entry.summary: Proposes Channel-Aware Probing (CAP) for multi-channel imaging that exploits channel structure when probing frozen pre-trained encoders, addressing the failure of standard probing strategies transferred from other domains.

entry.title: Adaptive Structured Pruning of Convolutional Neural Networks for Time Series Classification

author.name: Javidan Abdullayev, Maxime Devanne, Cyril Meyer, Ali Ismail-Fawaz, Jonathan Weber, Germain Forestier

entry.summary: Proposes Dynamic Structured Pruning (DSP) for convolution-based time series classification models with automatic pruning ratio determination through instance-wise sparsity loss and global activation analysis.

entry.title: Media Framing Moderates Risk-Benefit Perceptions and Value Tradeoffs in Human-Robot Collaboration

author.name: Philipp Brauner, Felix Glawe, Luisa Vervier, Martina Ziefle

entry.summary: Pre-registered study (N=1150) examining how positive/negative media framing moderates risk-benefit perceptions of human-robot collaboration in industrial settings. Finds framing significantly shifts how individuals evaluate HRC value.

entry.title: Can Neural Networks Provide Latent Embeddings for Telemetry-Aware Greedy Routing?

author.name: Andreas Boltres, Niklas Freymuth, Gerhard Neumann

entry.summary: Proposes Placer, a Message Passing Network algorithm that transforms network states into latent node embeddings for greedy routing, avoiding black-box routing decisions while enabling telemetry-aware routing visualization.

entry.title: X-VORTEX: Spatio-Temporal Contrastive Learning for Wake Vortex Trajectory Forecasting

author.name: Zhan Qu and Michael F\"arber

entry.summary: Presents X-VORTEX, a contrastive learning framework for wake vortex trajectory forecasting from LiDAR, leveraging augmentation overlap theory to learn physics-aware representations from unlabeled data.

entry.title: Robustness of Object Detection of Autonomous Vehicles in Adverse Weather Conditions

author.name: Fox Pettersen and Hong Zhu

entry.summary: Proposes a method for evaluating robustness of autonomous vehicle object detection under adverse weather using synthetic augmented data at progressive intensity levels, measuring average first failure coefficients.

entry.title: Curriculum Learning and Pseudo-Labeling Improve the Generalization of Multi-Label Arabic Dialect Identification Models

author.name: Ali Mekky, Mohamed El Zeftawy, Lara Hassan, Amr Keleg, Preslav Nakov

entry.summary: Addresses multi-label Arabic dialect identification using curriculum learning and pseudo-labeling with GPT-4o to generate automatic multi-label annotations from single-label datasets, improving generalization.

entry.title: Ca-MCF: Category-level Multi-label Causal Feature selection

author.name: Wanfu Gao, Yanan Wang, Yonghao Li

entry.summary: Introduces Ca-MCF for category-level multi-label causal feature selection that decomposes label variables into specific category nodes, enabling finer-grained causal structure modeling.

entry.title: Jointly Optimizing Debiased CTR and Uplift for Coupons Marketing: A Unified Causal Framework

author.name: Siyun Yang, Shixiao Yang, Jian Wang, Di Fan, Kehe Cai, Haoyan Fu, Jiaming Zhang, Wenjin Wu, Peng Jiang

entry.summary: Proposes UniMVT for jointly optimizing debiased CTR prediction and uplift estimation in coupon marketing, disentangling confounding factors from treatment-sensitive representations for counterfactual inference.

entry.title: Drift-Aware Variational Autoencoder-based Anomaly Detection with Two-level Ensembling

author.name: Jin Li, Kleanthis Malialis, Christos G. Panayiotou, Marios M. Polycarpou

entry.summary: Presents VAE++ESDD for anomaly detection in streaming data under concept drift, combining an ensemble of VAEs with an ensemble of statistical drift detectors for incremental learning.

entry.title: Resource-Efficient Gesture Recognition through Convexified Attention

author.name: Daniel Schwartz, Dario Salvucci, Yusuf Osmanlioglu, Richard Vallett, Genevieve Dion, and Ali Shokoufandeh

entry.summary: Introduces a convexified attention mechanism for wearable e-textile gesture recognition that uses simplex projection and convex loss functions instead of softmax, providing global convergence guarantees with minimal parameters for resource-constrained devices.

entry.title: EXCODER: EXplainable Classification Of DiscretE time series Representations

author.name: Yannik Hahn, Antonin K\"onigsfeld, Hasan Tercan, Tobias Meisen

entry.summary: Investigates whether transforming time series into discrete latent representations via VQ-VAE and DVAE enhances explainability of time series classification models by reducing redundancy and focusing on informative patterns.

entry.title: Eventizing Traditionally Opaque Binary Neural Networks as 1-safe Petri net Models

author.name: Mohamed Tarraf, Alex Chan, Alex Yakovlev and Rishad Shafik

entry.summary: Proposes modeling Binary Neural Networks as 1-safe Petri nets to expose causal relationships and enable formal verification of BNN internal operations as event-driven processes.

entry.title: Doctor-in-the-Loop: An Explainable, Multi-View Deep Learning Framework for Predicting Pathological Response in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer

author.name: Alice Natalina Caragliano, Filippo Ruffini, Carlo Greco, Edy Ippolito, Michele Fiore, Claudia Tacconi, Lorenzo Nibid, Giuseppe Perrone, Sara Ramella, Paolo Soda, Valerio Guarrasi

entry.summary: Proposes Doctor-in-the-Loop, a framework integrating expert domain knowledge with explainable AI for predicting pathological response in non-small cell lung cancer. Uses gradual multi-view strategy to focus on clinically relevant regions.

entry.title: Large Language Models for Healthcare Text Classification: A Systematic Review

author.name: Hajar Sakai and Sarah S. Lam

entry.summary: Systematic review of large language models applied to healthcare text classification, covering clinical notes, diagnosis coding, and related tasks. Surveys challenges including data privacy, medical terminology, and annotation scarcity.

entry.title: Beyond a Single Mode: GAN Ensembles for Diverse Medical Data Generation

author.name: Lorenzo Tronchin, Tommy L\"ofstedt, Paolo Soda, Valerio Guarrasi

entry.summary: Explores GAN ensembles to address mode collapse in medical image generation through multi-objective optimization balancing fidelity and diversity. Proposes optimal ensemble selection method for diverse synthetic medical data.

entry.title: Out of Distribution Detection for Efficient Continual Learning in Quality Prediction for Arc Welding

author.name: Yannik Hahn, Jan Voets, Antonin Koenigsfeld, Hasan Tercan, Tobias Meisen

entry.summary: Extends VQ-VAE Transformer architecture for weld quality prediction with OOD detection using autoregressive loss, combined with continual learning for adapting to distribution shifts in manufacturing.

entry.title: KORAL: Knowledge Graph Guided LLM Reasoning for SSD Operational Analysis

author.name: Mayur Akewar and Sandeep Madireddy and Dongsheng Luo and Janki Bhimani

entry.summary: Presents KORAL, a framework combining LLMs with knowledge graphs for SSD operational analysis, generating insights from fragmented telemetry data without requiring large datasets or expert input.

entry.title: Predicting Dynamic Map States from Limited Field-of-View Sensor Data

author.name: Knut Peterson and David Han

entry.summary: Explores deep learning for predicting dynamic map states from limited field-of-view sensor data, representing temporal sensor data in a single-image format for use with image-to-image learning models.

entry.title: Regularized Meta-Learning for Improved Generalization

author.name: Noor Islam S. Mohammad, Md Muntaqim Meherab

entry.summary: Proposes a regularized meta-learning framework addressing redundancy, multicollinearity, and overfitting in deep ensemble methods through a four-stage pipeline with redundancy-aware projection and statistical meta-feature augmentation.

entry.title: Matching of SAR and optical images based on transformation to shared modality

author.name: Alexey Borisov, Evgeny Myasnikov, Vladislav Myasnikov

entry.summary: Proposes a new approach for matching SAR and optical satellite images by transforming both into a shared modality that minimizes cross-modal differences while preserving geometric information.

entry.title: RoadscapesQA: A Multitask, Multimodal Dataset for Visual Question Answering on Indian Roads

author.name: Vijayasri Iyer, Maahin Rathinagiriswaran, Jyothikamalesh S

entry.summary: Presents RoadscapesQA, a multimodal VQA dataset of up to 9,000 images from diverse Indian driving environments with bounding boxes and rule-based QA pairs for object grounding, reasoning, and scene understanding.

entry.title: ViMedCSS: A Vietnamese Medical Code-Switching Speech Dataset & Benchmark

author.name: Tung X. Nguyen, Nhu Vo, Giang-Son Nguyen, Duy Mai Hoang, Chien Dinh Huynh, Inigo Jauregi Unanue, Massimo Piccardi, Wray Buntine, Dung D. Le

entry.summary: Constructs ViMedCSS, a 34-hour Vietnamese medical code-switching speech dataset with 16,576 utterances for evaluating ASR systems on Vietnamese-English medical code-switching.

entry.title: Multi-Dimensional Visual Data Recovery: Scale-Aware Tensor Modeling and Accelerated Randomized Computation

author.name: Wenjin Qin, Hailin Wang, Jiangjun Peng, Jianjun Wang, and Tingwen Huang

entry.summary: Proposes generalized nonconvex regularization and scalable recovery models for multi-dimensional data using fully-connected tensor network decomposition, with randomized computation for efficiency.

entry.title: Synaptic Activation and Dual Liquid Dynamics for Interpretable Bio-Inspired Models

author.name: M\'onika Farsang, Radu Grosu

entry.summary: Presents a unified framework for bio-inspired neural network models incorporating chemical synapses and dual liquid dynamics, demonstrating improved interpretability in recurrent neural network policies for lane-keeping control tasks.

entry.title: Barron-Wiener-Laguerre models

author.name: Rahul Manavalan, Filip Tronarp

entry.summary: Proposes probabilistic Wiener-Laguerre models that combine Laguerre-parameterized causal dynamics with Barron-type nonlinear maps for operator learning, enabling Bayesian inference and posterior predictive uncertainty.

entry.title: OpenLID-v3: Improving the Precision of Closely Related Language Identification -- An Experience Report

author.name: Mariia Fedorova, Nikolay Arefyev, Maja Buljan, Jind\v{r}ich Helcl, Stephan Oepen, Egil R{\o}nningstad, Yves Scherrer

entry.summary: Extends the OpenLID language identification classifier to handle closely related languages better and distinguish valid language from noise, focusing on Scandinavian, Balkan, and Romance language groups.

entry.title: Whole-Body Image-to-Image Translation for a Virtual Scanner in a Healthcare Digital Twin

author.name: Valerio Guarrasi, Francesco Di Feola, Rebecca Restivo, Lorenzo Tronchin, Paolo Soda

entry.summary: Proposes a framework for whole-body CT-to-PET image translation using region-specific GANs for head, trunk, arms, and legs, then stitching results together. Aims to reduce radiation exposure from PET imaging.

entry.title: Multimodal Doctor-in-the-Loop: A Clinically-Guided Explainable Framework for Predicting Pathological Response in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer

author.name: Alice Natalina Caragliano, Claudia Tacconi, Carlo Greco, Lorenzo Nibid, Edy Ippolito, Michele Fiore, Giuseppe Perrone, Sara Ramella, Paolo Soda, and Valerio Guarrasi

entry.summary: Extends Doctor-in-the-Loop to a multimodal setting, combining imaging and clinical data with intermediate fusion for predicting pathological response in NSCLC. Embeds clinician domain knowledge into training.

entry.title: Class Balancing Diversity Multimodal Ensemble for Alzheimer's Disease Diagnosis and Early Detection

author.name: Arianna Francesconi, Lazzaro di Biase, Donato Cappetta, Fabio Rebecchi, Paolo Soda, Rosa Sicilia, Valerio Guarrasi

entry.summary: Proposes IMBALMED, a multimodal ensemble method for Alzheimer's disease diagnosis that handles class imbalance by integrating clinical, neuroimaging, biospecimen, and subject data. Uses ensemble of classifiers with class-balancing diversity optimization.

entry.title: Texture-Aware StarGAN for CT data harmonisation

author.name: Francesco Di Feola, Ludovica Pompilio, Cecilia Assolito, Valerio Guarrasi, Paolo Soda

entry.summary: Proposes a texture-aware StarGAN for harmonizing CT data across different reconstruction kernels. Uses texture-aware loss to better capture complex image relationships for style transfer in medical imaging.

entry.title: Exploring the robustness of TractOracle methods in RL-based tractography

author.name: Jeremi Levesque, Antoine Th\'eberge, Maxime Descoteaux, Pierre-Marc Jodoin

entry.summary: Investigates extensions to TractOracle-RL for brain white matter tractography, integrating recent RL advances and evaluating across five diffusion MRI datasets. Shows that oracle-guided RL consistently yields robust tractography.

entry.title: Evaluating the Creativity of LLMs in Persian Literary Text Generation

author.name: Armin Tourajmehr, Mohammad Reza Modarres, Yadollah Yaghoobzadeh

entry.summary: Evaluates LLMs' ability to generate creative Persian literary text using adapted Torrance Tests of Creative Thinking. Uses LLM-as-judge with human validation across originality, fluency, flexibility, and elaboration dimensions.

entry.title: Wireless TokenCom: RL-Based Tokenizer Agreement for Multi-User Wireless Token Communications

author.name: Farshad Zeinali, Mahdi Boloursaz Mashhadi, Dusit Niyato, Rahim Tafazolli

entry.summary: Introduces a reinforcement learning framework for tokenizer agreement in multi-user wireless token communications, where transmitters and receivers cooperate to choose optimal tokenizer models for semantic communication.

entry.title: Thermal Imaging for Contactless Cardiorespiratory and Sudomotor Response Monitoring

author.name: Constantino \'Alvarez Casado, Mohammad Rahman, Sasan Sharifipour, Nhi Nguyen, Manuel Lage Ca\~nellas, Xiaoting Wu, Miguel Bordallo L\'opez

entry.summary: Characterizes extraction of EDA, heart rate, and breathing rate from facial thermal video using signal processing pipelines. Provides contactless monitoring of cardiorespiratory and sudomotor responses.

entry.title: Accelerating Feedback-based Algorithms for Quantum Optimization Using Gradient Descent

author.name: Masih Mozakka, Mohsen Heidari

entry.summary: Proposes a hybrid method combining per-layer gradient estimation with Quantum Lyapunov Control to accelerate convergence of QAOA while preserving stability guarantees for combinatorial optimization.

entry.title: Reproducing DragDiffusion: Interactive Point-Based Editing with Diffusion Models

author.name: Ali Subhan, Ashir Raza

entry.summary: A reproducibility study of DragDiffusion for interactive point-based image editing. Confirms original ablation results but reveals sensitivity to hyperparameters and failure modes not discussed in the original paper.

entry.title: Neural and numerical methods for $\mathrm{G}_2$-structures on contact Calabi-Yau 7-manifolds

author.name: Elli Heyes, Edward Hirst, Henrique N. S\'a Earp, Tom\'as S. R. Silva

entry.summary: Presents a numerical framework using neural networks to approximate G₂-structure 3-forms on contact Calabi-Yau manifolds, computing approximate Ricci-flat metrics and validating learned structures via numerical exterior derivative.

entry.title: Probabilistic Design of Parametrized Quantum Circuits through Local Gate Modifications

author.name: Grier M. Jones, Aviraj Newatia, Alexander Lao, Aditya K. Rao, Viki Kumar Prasad, Hans-Arno Jacobsen

entry.summary: Proposes a local quantum architecture search algorithm using evolution-inspired probabilistic gate-level modifications to optimize parametrized quantum circuits for quantum machine learning tasks.

entry.title: Analytical Results for Two Exponential Family Distributions in Hierarchical Dirichlet Processes

author.name: Naiqi Li

entry.summary: Derives closed-form expressions for Poisson and normal distributions within the Hierarchical Dirichlet Process framework, extending analytical tractability beyond the standard Dirichlet-multinomial conjugate case.

entry.title: CLASE: A Hybrid Method for Chinese Legalese Stylistic Evaluation

author.name: Yiran Rex Ma, Yuxiao Ye, Huiyuan Xie

entry.summary: Introduces CLASE, a hybrid method for evaluating the stylistic quality of Chinese legal text generated by LLMs. Addresses the gap between factual accuracy and adherence to specialized legal writing conventions that are hard to formalize explicitly.

entry.title: Multi-Task Learning with Additive U-Net for Image Denoising and Classification

author.name: Vikram Lakkavalli and Neelam Sinha

entry.summary: Investigates additive skip fusion in U-Net architectures for image denoising and multi-task learning, replacing concatenative skips with gated additive fusion. Shows task-aware redistribution of skip weights in joint denoising-classification settings.

entry.title: "Not Human, Funnier": How Machine Identity Shapes Humor Perception in Online AI Stand-up Comedy

author.name: Xuehan Huang, Canwen Wang, Yifei Hao, Daijin Yang, Ray LC

entry.summary: Explores how AI's own machine identity can be leveraged for humor generation in stand-up comedy. Studies with human audiences (N=32) showed machine-identity-based agents were perceived as funnier than baseline GPT, suggesting identity-aware comedy design for AI.

entry.title: Knowledge-Based Design Requirements for Generative Social Robots in Higher Education

author.name: Stephan Vonschallen, Dominique Oberle, Theresa Schmiedel, and Friederike Eyssel

entry.summary: Investigates knowledge requirements for generative social robots powered by LLMs in higher education, identifying twelve design requirements across self-knowledge, context-knowledge, and world-knowledge from interviews with students and lecturers.

entry.title: Adaptive Scaling with Geometric and Visual Continuity of completed 3D objects

author.name: Jelle Vermandere, Maarten Bassier, Maarten Vergauwen

entry.summary: Introduces a part-aware scaling framework that transforms static completed SDFs into editable objects with smooth interpolation of geometry, color, and part indices for proportional deformation.

entry.title: Evaluating the Homogeneity of Keyphrase Prediction Models

author.name: Ma\"el Houbre, Florian Boudin, Beatrice Daille

entry.summary: Evaluates homogeneity of keyphrase prediction models, testing whether generation models are more consistent than extraction models in assigning the same keyphrases to documents about the same subjects.

entry.title: Probabilistic Wind Power Forecasting with Tree-Based Machine Learning and Weather Ensembles

author.name: Max Bruninx, Diederik van Binsbergen, Timothy Verstraeten, Ann Now\'e, Jan Helsen

entry.summary: Compares three probabilistic prediction methods (conformal quantile regression, natural gradient boosting, conditional diffusion models) for day-ahead wind power forecasting using gradient boosting trees with weather ensemble data. Validated on four years of Belgian offshore wind farm data. Applied ML work for renewable energy integration.

entry.title: Towards a Neuronally Consistent Ontology for Robotic Agents

author.name: Florian Ahrens, Mihai Pomarlan, Daniel Be{\ss}ler, Thorsten Fehr, Michael Beetz, Manfred Herrmann

entry.summary: Proposes using human neuroimaging data (ICA on fMRI) to validate and enrich ontologies used by robotic agents, bridging neuroscience and robot knowledge representation. The goal is to help robots learn from human experiences by grounding ontological concepts in neural information processing.

entry.title: A Model-Driven Engineering Approach to AI-Powered Healthcare Platforms

author.name: Mira Raheem, Amal Elgammal, Michael Papazoglou, Bernd Kr\"amer, Neamat El-Tazi

entry.summary: Introduces a model-driven engineering framework for healthcare AI using formal metamodels and domain-specific languages, including MILA for clinicians to define ML pipelines using shared ontologies.

entry.title: Quantum walk inspired JPEG compression of images

author.name: Abhishek Verma, Sahil Tomar, Sandeep Kumar

entry.summary: Proposes a quantum walk-inspired optimization strategy for adaptive JPEG quantization tables, showing 3-6 dB PSNR gains over standard JPEG on MNIST, CIFAR10, and ImageNet subsets.

entry.title: Geometric Stratification for Singular Configurations of the P3P Problem via Local Dual Space

author.name: Xueying Sun, Zijia Li, Nan Li

entry.summary: Provides complete geometric stratification of singular configurations in the P3P (Perspective-three-Point) problem using local dual space, relating multiplicity of camera center to geometric structures like the danger cylinder.

entry.title: Lung nodule classification on CT scan patches using 3D convolutional neural networks

author.name: Volodymyr Sydorskyi

entry.summary: Introduces three improvements for lung nodule classification on CT scans using 3D CNNs: advanced preprocessing, architecture modifications, and training strategies. Addresses the need for efficient automated lung cancer screening.

entry.title: AIWizards at MULTIPRIDE: A Hierarchical Approach to Slur Reclamation Detection

author.name: Luca Tedeschini, Matteo Fasulo

entry.summary: Proposes a hierarchical approach for detecting reclaimed slurs in LGBTQ+ contexts, using weakly supervised LLM-based annotation of user identity followed by slur classification. Addresses the EVALITA 2026 MultiPRIDE shared task.

entry.title: SKYSURF: A Self-learning Framework for Persistent Surveillance using Cooperative Aerial Gliders

author.name: Houssem Eddine Mohamadi, Nadjia Kara

entry.summary: Proposes a behavioral management approach for autonomous soaring-capable UAVs modeled as finite state-based rational agents, using delayed learning and tuning for cooperative surveillance in thermal updrafts.

entry.title: Never say never: Exploring the effects of available knowledge on agent persuasiveness in controlled physiotherapy motivation dialogues

author.name: Stephan Vonschallen, Rahel H\"ausler, Theresa Schmiedel, and Friederike Eyssel

entry.summary: Explores how available knowledge affects persuasiveness of ChatGPT-generated messages in physiotherapy motivation contexts, comparing responses across different knowledge configurations in human-robot interaction.

entry.title: Learning Image-based Tree Crown Segmentation from Enhanced Lidar-based Pseudo-labels

author.name: Julius Pesonen, Stefan Rua, Josef Taher, Niko Koivum\"aki, Xiaowei Yu, Eija Honkavaara

entry.summary: Presents a method to train deep learning models for individual tree crown segmentation from aerial imagery using pseudo-labels derived from lidar data, enhanced by SAM 2. Demonstrates practical approach for environmental monitoring.

entry.title: Implicit-Scale 3D Reconstruction for Multi-Food Volume Estimation from Monocular Images

author.name: Yuhao Chen, Gautham Vinod, Siddeshwar Raghavan, Talha Ibn Mahmud, Bruce Coburn, Jinge Ma, Fengqing Zhu and Jiangpeng He

entry.summary: Presents a benchmark dataset for food volume estimation reframed as implicit-scale 3D reconstruction from monocular images, where algorithms must infer scale from contextual cues like plates and utensils rather than explicit references.

entry.title: Exploring a New Competency Modeling Process with Large Language Models

author.name: Silin Du, Manqing Xin, Raymond Jia Wang

entry.summary: Proposes using LLMs to automate competency modeling in HR management, replacing manual expert analysis of interview transcripts with structured computational workflows using embedding-based similarity mapping.

entry.title: Constrained Assumption-Based Argumentation Frameworks

author.name: Emanuele De Angelis (1), Fabio Fioravanti (2), Maria Chiara Meo (2), Alberto Pettorossi (3), Maurizio Proietti (1), Francesca Toni (4) ((1) CNR-IASI, Rome, Italy, (2) DEc, University 'G. d'Annunzio', Chieti-Pescara, Italy, (3) DICII, University of Rome 'Tor Vergata', Italy, (4) Imperial, London, UK)

entry.summary: Proposes Constrained ABA (CABA), extending Assumption-Based Argumentation to support constrained variables over possibly infinite domains, with non-ground semantics that generalize standard ABA.

entry.title: Temporally-Sampled Efficiently Adaptive State Lattices for Autonomous Ground Robot Navigation in Partially Observed Environments

author.name: Ashwin Satish Menon (1), Eric R. Damm (1), Eli S. Lancaster (2), Felix A. Sanchez (3), Jason M. Gregory (2), Thomas M. Howard (1 and 2) ((1) University of Rochester, (2) DEVCOM Army Research Lab, (3) Parsons Corporation)

entry.summary: Proposes a temporal sampling approach for state lattice planning in partially observed off-road environments, addressing unsafe navigation behavior caused by rapidly changing regional plan guidance.

entry.title: Monocular Markerless Motion Capture Enables Quantitative Assessment of Upper Extremity Reachable Workspace

author.name: Seth Donahue, J.D. Peiffer, R. Tyler Richardson, Yishan Zhong, Shaun Q. Y. Tan, Benoit Marteau, Stephanie R. Russo, May D. Wang, R. James Cotton, Ross Chafetz

entry.summary: Validates monocular markerless motion capture using AI for quantifying upper extremity reachable workspace, comparing against marker-based systems in a clinical assessment context.

entry.title: Multi-Dataset Multi-Task Learning for COVID-19 Prognosis

author.name: Filippo Ruffini, Lorenzo Tronchin, Zhuoru Wu, Wenting Chen, Paolo Soda, Linlin Shen, Valerio Guarrasi

entry.summary: Introduces a multi-dataset multi-task training framework for predicting COVID-19 prognosis from chest X-rays by integrating correlated datasets from different sources. Addresses data scarcity by combining severity scoring with prognostic classification.

entry.title: Adaptive traffic signal control optimization using a novel road partition and multi-channel state representation method

author.name: Maojiang Deng, Shoufeng Lu, Jiazhao Shi, Wen Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes a DQN/PPO-based adaptive traffic signal control using variable cell length road partitioning and multi-channel state representation with vehicle count, speed, and occupancy.

entry.title: A consequence of failed sequential learning: A computational account of developmental amnesia

author.name: Qi Zhang

entry.summary: Presents a computational model of developmental amnesia demonstrating impaired episodic recall with spared recognition and semantic learning, attributing it to failed sequential/spatial learning in the hippocampus.

entry.title: Vehicle behaviour estimation for abnormal event detection using distributed fiber optic sensing

author.name: Hemant Prasad, Daisuke Ikefuji, Shin Tominaga, Hitoshi Sakurai, Manabu Otani

entry.summary: Presents a method for detecting single-lane traffic abnormalities using distributed fiber-optic sensing by tracking individual vehicle paths and detecting lane changes through clustering techniques. This enables early detection of congestion causes.

entry.title: Synthetic Craquelure Generation for Unsupervised Painting Restoration

author.name: Jana Cuch-Guill\'en, Antonio Agudo, Ra\"ul P\'erez-Gonzalo

entry.summary: Proposes a fully annotation-free framework for painting craquelure detection and restoration using synthetic crack generation with Bézier trajectories, combined with a SegFormer backbone adapted via LoRA.

entry.title: BaziQA-Benchmark: Evaluating Symbolic and Temporally Compositional Reasoning in Large Language Models

author.name: Jiangxi Chen and Qian Liu

entry.summary: Presents BaziQA-Benchmark for evaluating symbolic and temporally compositional reasoning in LLMs, derived from 200 fortune-telling competition problems requiring structured inference over symbolic charts.

entry.title: MAUNet-Light: A Concise MAUNet Architecture for Bias Correction and Downscaling of Precipitation Estimates

author.name: Sumanta Chandra Mishra Sharma, Adway Mitra, Auroop Ratan Ganguly

entry.summary: Proposes MAUNet-Light, a compact version of the MAUNet architecture for precipitation bias correction and downscaling, achieving competitive performance with fewer parameters.

entry.title: Represent Micro-Doppler Signature in Orders

author.name: Weicheng Gao

entry.summary: Proposes Chebyshev-time maps for representing micro-Doppler signatures from through-wall radar using polynomial orders, reducing input dimensionality while maintaining discriminative power.

entry.title: How Swarms Differ: Challenges in Collective Behaviour Comparison

author.name: Andr\'e Fialho Jesus and Jonas Kuckling

entry.summary: Investigates how different feature sets and similarity measures affect the comparison of collective swarm behaviors in robotics, finding that existing ad-hoc feature sets lack robustness across behavioral contexts.

entry.title: From sunblock to softblock: Analyzing the correlates of neology in published writing and on social media

author.name: Maria Ryskina, Matthew R. Gormley, Kyle Mahowald, David R. Mortensen, Taylor Berg-Kirkpatrick, Vivek Kulkarni

entry.summary: Analyzes correlates of new word creation (neology) using distributional semantics, extending methodology from historical published texts to Twitter data and from static to contextual embeddings.

entry.title: Optimal Take-off under Fuzzy Clearances

author.name: Hugo Henry and Arthur Tsai and Kelly Cohen

entry.summary: Presents a hybrid obstacle avoidance system for unmanned aircraft combining fuzzy logic for adaptive constraint handling with optimal control, using FAA/EASA guidelines to modulate safety parameters.

entry.title: A Lightweight Cubature Kalman Filter for Attitude and Heading Reference Systems Using Simplified Prediction Equations

author.name: Shunsei Yamagishi, Lei Jing

entry.summary: Presents KCKF, a lightweight Cubature Kalman Filter for attitude estimation that reduces computational cost by ~19% through simplification of prediction equations while maintaining accuracy.

entry.title: VineetVC: Adaptive Video Conferencing Under Severe Bandwidth Constraints Using Audio-Driven Talking-Head Reconstruction

author.name: Vineet Kumar Rakesh and Soumya Mazumdar and Tapas Samanta and Hemendra Kumar Pandey and Amitabha Das and Sarbajit Pal

entry.summary: Describes an adaptive video conferencing system that switches to audio-driven talking-head reconstruction when bandwidth drops severely, using WebRTC telemetry to trigger mode transitions.

entry.title: Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis for Future Tourism Experiences: A BERT-MoE Framework for Persian User Reviews

author.name: Hamidreza Kazemi Taskooh and Taha Zare Harofte

entry.summary: Proposes a BERT-MoE hybrid model for aspect-based sentiment analysis of Persian tourism reviews, achieving 90.6% weighted F1. Addresses low-resource language challenges with a dataset of 58K reviews from an Iranian platform.

entry.title: A Microservice-Based Platform for Sustainable and Intelligent SLO Fulfilment and Service Management

author.name: Juan Luis Herrera, Daniel Wang, Schahram Dustdar

entry.summary: Proposes a microservice-based platform for sustainable SLO fulfillment using intelligent decision systems across the Computing Continuum, addressing the tension between performance and sustainability objectives.

entry.title: Machine Learning-Based Classification of Jhana Advanced Concentrative Absorption Meditation (ACAM-J) using 7T fMRI

author.name: Puneet Kumar, Winson F. Z. Yang, Alakhsimar Singh, Xiaobai Li, and Matthew D. Sacchet

entry.summary: Uses 7T fMRI and machine learning to classify Jhana advanced meditation states from regional homogeneity features, evaluating generalization from group-level training to intensive single-case data.

entry.title: Towards interpretable models for language proficiency assessment: Predicting the CEFR level of Estonian learner texts

author.name: Kais Allkivi

entry.summary: Classifies Estonian proficiency examination writings by CEFR level using interpretable linguistic features, comparing traditional ML models with LLM-based approaches for language proficiency assessment.

entry.title: String-Level Ground Fault Localization for TN-Earthed Three-Phase Photovoltaic Systems

author.name: Yuanliang Li, Xun Gong, Reza Iravani, Bo Cao, Heng Liu, Ziming Chen

entry.summary: Presents an edge-AI approach for localizing ground faults in three-phase photovoltaic systems at string level, using simulation-generated features and correlation-based analysis.

entry.title: A Gradient Boosted Mixed-Model Machine Learning Framework for Vessel Speed in the U.S. Arctic

author.name: Mauli Pant, Linda Fernandez, Indranil Sahoo

entry.summary: Applies a two-stage gradient boosted machine learning framework with random effects to model vessel speed in U.S. Arctic waters using AIS data, accounting for zero-speed observations.

entry.title: Interference-Robust Non-Coherent Over-the-Air Computation for Decentralized Optimization

author.name: Nicol\`o Michelusi

entry.summary: Proposes an interference-robust non-coherent over-the-air computation method for decentralized optimization in wireless networks, addressing the susceptibility of NCOTA to external interference.

entry.title: Constrained PSO Six-Parameter Fuzzy PID Tuning Method for Balanced Optimization of Depth Tracking Performance in Underwater Vehicles

author.name: Yanxi Ding and Tingyue Jia

entry.summary: Proposes constrained PSO for tuning six-parameter fuzzy PID controllers for underwater vehicle depth control, optimizing tracking performance while satisfying actuator constraints.

entry.title: ART3mis: Ray-Based Textual Annotation on 3D Cultural Objects

author.name: Vasileios Arampatzakis, Vasileios Sevetlidis, Fotis Arnaoutoglou, Athanasios Kalogeras, Christos Koulamas, Aris Lalos, Chairi Kiourt, George Ioannakis, Anestis Koutsoudis, George Pavlidis

entry.summary: Presents ART3mis, a ray-based interactive tool for annotating textual metadata onto specific regions of 3D cultural heritage objects. Designed for cultural heritage professionals without 3D graphics expertise.

entry.title: Towards complete digital twins in cultural heritage with ART3mis 3D artifacts annotator

author.name: Dimitrios Karamatskos, Vasileios Arampatzakis, Vasileios Sevetlidis, Stavros Nousias, Athanasios Kalogeras, Christos Koulamas, Aris Lalos, George Pavlidis

entry.summary: Presents ART3mis, a web-based 3D annotation tool for cultural heritage objects compliant with W3C Web Annotation Data Model. Enables non-technical cultural heritage practitioners to annotate and attach metadata to specific regions of 3D objects.

entry.title: Semantic Communities and Boundary-Spanning Lyrics in K-pop: A Graph-Based Unsupervised Analysis

author.name: Oktay Karaku\c{s}

entry.summary: Presents a graph-based unsupervised framework for discovering semantic communities in K-pop lyrics using line-level semantic representations and community detection, identifying boundary-spanning songs via bridge metrics.

entry.title: Human Emotion-Mediated Soft Robotic Arts: Exploring the Intersection of Human Emotions, Soft Robotics and Arts

author.name: Saitarun Nadipineni, Chenhao Hong, Tanishtha Ramlall, Chapa Sirithunge, Kaspar Althoefer, Fumiya Iida and Thilina Dulantha Lalitharatne

entry.summary: Explores soft robotic art installations that dynamically respond to human brain signals (alpha waves) to create emotion-mediated interactive displays using soft characters and flowers.

entry.title: Selection of CMIP6 Models for Regional Precipitation Projection and Climate Change Assessment in the Jhelum and Chenab River Basins

author.name: Saad Ahmed Jamal, Ammara Nusrat, Muhammad Azmat, Muhammad Osama Nusrat

entry.summary: Selects CMIP6 climate models for precipitation projection in Pakistan river basins using envelope-based method with ML techniques, studying climate change effects under SSP scenarios.

entry.title: Visible and Hyperspectral Imaging for Quality Assessment of Milk: Property Characterisation and Identification

author.name: Massimo Martinelli, Elena Tomassi, Nafiou Arouna, Morena Gabriele, Laryssa Perez Fabbri, Luisa Pozzo, Giuseppe Conte, Davide Moroni, Laura Pucci

entry.summary: Investigates visible and hyperspectral imaging combined with machine learning for non-destructive assessment of cow's milk quality, comparing 11 ML methods on 52 milk samples.

entry.title: Grandes Modelos de Linguagem Multimodais (MLLMs): Da Teoria \`a Pr\'atica

author.name: Neemias da Silva, J\'ulio C. W. Scholz, John Harrison, Marina Borges, Paulo \'Avila, Frances A Santos, Myriam Delgado, Rodrigo Minetto and Thiago H Silva

entry.summary: Portuguese-language tutorial/chapter on Multimodal Large Language Models covering fundamentals, practical techniques with LangChain/LangGraph, and prompt engineering. Includes supplementary code.

entry.title: TFT-ACB-XML: Decision-Level Integration of Customized Temporal Fusion Transformer and Attention-BiLSTM with XGBoost Meta-Learner for BTC Price Forecasting

author.name: Raiz Ud Din (1), Saddam Hussain Khan (2) ((1) Artificial Intelligence Lab, Department of Computer Systems Engineering, University of Engineering and Applied Sciences (UEAS), Swat, Pakistan, (2) Interdisciplinary Research Center for Smart Mobility and Logistics, King Fahad University of Petroleum and Minerals (KFUPM), Dhahran, Saudi Arabia)

entry.summary: Proposes TFT-ACB-XML, a hybrid framework combining Temporal Fusion Transformer, Attention-BiLSTM, and XGBoost meta-learner for Bitcoin price prediction.

entry.title: A Lightweight and Explainable DenseNet-121 Framework for Grape Leaf Disease Classification

author.name: Md. Ehsanul Haque, Md.Saymon Hosen Polash, Rakib Hasan Ovi, Aminul Kader Bulbul, Md Kamrul Siam, Tamim Hasan Saykat

entry.summary: Proposes an optimized DenseNet-121 framework with explainability for grape leaf disease classification, using domain-specific preprocessing and Grad-CAM visualizations.

author.name: Flavio Dell Acqua, Maxime Descoteaux, Graham Little, Laurent Petit, Dogu Baran Aydogan, Stephanie Forkel, Alexander Leemans, Simona Schiavi, Michel Thiebaut de Schotten

entry.summary: Conference proceedings abstracts from the inaugural International Society for Tractography conference, covering advances in tractography, diffusion MRI, neurological disorders, and brain development.

entry.title: Hemispherical Angular Power Mapping of Installed mmWave Radar Modules Under Realistic Deployment Constraints

author.name: Maaz Qureshi, Mohammad Omid Bagheri, William Melek, and George Shaker

entry.summary: Presents a methodology for hemispherical angular power mapping of installed mmWave radar modules under realistic deployment constraints.

entry.title: Research Summary: February 13, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research reveals critical vulnerabilities in both AI alignment and evaluation methodology, alongside fundamental theoretical advances in interpretability.

  • Capability-Oriented Training Induced Alignment Risk shows standard RL training spontaneously produces exploitation behaviors—a major safety finding without requiring adversarial setup
  • Benchmark Illusion demonstrates LLMs with similar accuracy disagree on 16–66% of individual items, undermining benchmark-driven scientific conclusions
  • Retrieval-Aware Distillation from Albert Gu's group finds just 2% of attention heads suffice to preserve retrieval in Transformer-to-SSM hybrid conversion
  • A rigorous proof under the Linear Representation Hypothesis establishes that O(m^(4/3)) neurons can linearly encode features, advancing interpretability theory

In robotics and reasoning, Scaling Verification for VLA Alignment from Stanford/Google shows test-time verification outperforms policy scaling for robot action alignment. Native Reasoning Training breaks the verifiable-reward bottleneck by training reasoning on unverifiable tasks. Audio-LLMs exhibit stark text dominance, following text over audio 10x more often in cross-modal conflict.

  • Direction vs. Magnitude dissociation in transformer representations reveals angular perturbations damage language modeling while magnitude perturbations damage classification—a clean double dissociation
  • SafeNeuron redistributes safety across the network to resist fine-tuning attacks that exploit concentrated safety neurons
  • Dedicated Feature Crosscoders enable unsupervised cross-architecture model diffing, a new tool for comparing structurally different LLMs

entry.title: Capability-Oriented Training Induced Alignment Risk

author.name: Yujun Zhou, Yue Huang, Han Bao, Kehan Guo, Zhenwen Liang, Pin-Yu Chen, Tian Gao, Werner Geyer, Nuno Moniz, Nitesh V Chawla, Xiangliang Zhang

entry.summary: Investigates whether capability-oriented RL training causes LLMs to spontaneously exploit environmental loopholes to maximize reward, even without malicious training intent. Designs four 'vulnerability games' testing context-conditional compliance, proxy metrics, reward tampering, and self-evaluation exploitation. Shows models consistently discover and exploit these vulnerabilities.

entry.title: Benchmark Illusion: Disagreement among LLMs and Its Scientific Consequences

author.name: Eddie Yang, Dashun Wang

entry.summary: Reveals that LLMs achieving similar benchmark accuracy still disagree on 16-66% of individual items, and when used for scientific data annotation, switching models can change treatment effects by over 100% or flip statistical significance. Demonstrates that benchmark convergence masks deep epistemic divergence.

Subramanian, Soham Ghosh, Srijan Mishra, Abhinav Rastogi, Alan Jeffares, Albert Jiang, Alexandre Sablayrolles, Am\'elie H\'eliou, Andrew Bai, Angele Lenglemetz, Anmol Agarwal, Anton Eliseev, Antonia Simon Sorg, Thibaut Lavril, Thomas Chabal, Thomas Foubert, Thomas Robert, Thomas Wang, Tim Lawson, Tom Bewley, Tom Edwards, Tyler Wang, Valeriia Nemychnikova, Van Phung, Vedant Nanda, Victor Jouault, entry.summary: Introduces Voxtral Realtime, a natively streaming ASR model from Mistral that matches offline transcription quality (on par with Whisper) at sub-second latency (~480ms). Uses a new causal audio encoder and Ada RMS-Norm within a Delayed Streams Modeling framework, pretrained on 13 languages. Weights released under Apache 2.

entry.title: How Many Features Can a Language Model Store Under the Linear Representation Hypothesis?

author.name: Nikhil Garg, Jon Kleinberg, Kenny Peng

entry.summary: Provides a mathematical framework for the linear representation hypothesis (LRH) in language models, proving that O(m^(4/3)) neurons suffice to linearly represent and access m features, with a near-matching lower bound.

entry.title: Scaling Verification Can Be More Effective than Scaling Policy Learning for Vision-Language-Action Alignment

author.name: Jacky Kwok, Xilun Zhang, Mengdi Xu, Yuejiang Liu, Azalia Mirhoseini, Chelsea Finn, Marco Pavone

entry.summary: This paper investigates test-time verification as a way to close the gap between intended instructions and generated actions in Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models for robotics. They characterize test-time scaling laws for embodied instruction following and show that jointly scaling rephrased instructions and generated actions greatly increases sample diversity. Notable authors include Chelsea Finn, Marco Pavone, and Azalia Mirhoseini.

entry.title: Retrieval-Aware Distillation for Transformer-SSM Hybrids

author.name: Aviv Bick, Eric P. Xing, Albert Gu

entry.summary: Retrieval-aware distillation converts a pretrained Transformer into a hybrid Transformer-SSM model by preserving only 2% of attention heads (retrieval-critical 'Gather-and-Aggregate' heads) and distilling the rest into recurrent heads, recovering 95%+ performance on retrieval tasks.

entry.title: Latent Forcing: Reordering the Diffusion Trajectory for Pixel-Space Image Generation

author.name: Alan Baade, Eric Ryan Chan, Kyle Sargent, Changan Chen, Justin Johnson, Ehsan Adeli, Li Fei-Fei

entry.summary: Proposes Latent Forcing, which achieves efficiency of latent diffusion while operating on raw pixels by jointly processing latents and pixels with separate noise schedules. The latents serve as a scratchpad before high-frequency pixel features are generated. From Fei-Fei Li's group at Stanford.

entry.title: When Audio-LLMs Don't Listen: A Cross-Linguistic Study of Modality Arbitration

author.name: Jayadev Billa

entry.summary: Reveals that audio-LLMs like Gemini 2.0 Flash exhibit strong text dominance bias, following text 10x more often than audio when the two conflict, even when explicitly instructed to trust audio. Proposes that this reflects an asymmetry in arbitration accessibility rather than information quality.

entry.title: Artificial intelligence is creating a new global linguistic hierarchy

author.name: Giulia Occhini, Kumiko Tanaka-Ishii, Anna Barford, Refael Tikochinski, Songbo Hu, Roi Reichart, Yijie Zhou, Hannah Claus, Ulla Petti, Ivan Vuli\'c, Ramit Debnath, Anna Korhonen

entry.summary: Presents a global longitudinal analysis showing AI is creating a new linguistic hierarchy, with benefits concentrated in a small number of languages while most of the world's 7,000+ linguistic communities face digital marginalization.

entry.title: Causal-JEPA: Learning World Models through Object-Level Latent Interventions

author.name: Heejeong Nam, Quentin Le Lidec, Lucas Maes, Yann LeCun, Randall Balestriero

entry.summary: Proposes C-JEPA, an object-centric world model extending JEPA to object-level representations with masking that induces latent interventions for causal reasoning. Shows gains in visual QA tasks. Authors include Yann LeCun and Randall Balestriero.

entry.title: Gaia2: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Dynamic and Asynchronous Environments

author.name: Romain Froger, Pierre Andrews, Matteo Bettini, Amar Budhiraja, Ricardo Silveira Cabral, Virginie Do, Emilien Garreau, Jean-Baptiste Gaya, Hugo Lauren\c{c}on, Maxime Lecanu, Kunal Malkan, Dheeraj Mekala, Pierre M\'enard, Gerard Moreno-Torres Bertran, Ulyana Piterbarg, Mikhail Plekhanov, Mathieu Rita, Andrey Rusakov, Vladislav Vorotilov, Mengjue Wang, Ian Yu, Amine Benhalloum, Gr\'egoire Mialon, Thomas Scialom

entry.summary: Introduces Gaia2, a benchmark for evaluating LLM agents in dynamic, asynchronous environments where environments evolve independently of agent actions. Includes write-action verifiers for RL training. Tests GPT-5 and other SOTA models, finding no model dominates across all capabilities.

entry.title: Disentangling Direction and Magnitude in Transformer Representations: A Double Dissociation Through L2-Matched Perturbation Analysis

author.name: Mangadoddi Srikar Vardhan, Lekkala Sai Teja

entry.summary: Discovers a striking dissociation in transformer representations: angular (direction) perturbations damage language modeling while magnitude perturbations disproportionately damage syntactic processing, revealing distinct functional roles of direction and magnitude in Pythia models.

entry.title: MolmoSpaces: A Large-Scale Open Ecosystem for Robot Navigation and Manipulation

author.name: Yejin Kim, Wilbert Pumacay, Omar Rayyan, Max Argus, Winson Han, Eli VanderBilt, Jordi Salvador, Abhay Deshpande, Rose Hendrix, Snehal Jauhri, Shuo Liu, Nur Muhammad Mahi Shafiullah, Maya Guru, Ainaz Eftekhar, Karen Farley, Donovan Clay, Jiafei Duan, Arjun Guru, Piper Wolters, Alvaro Herrasti, Ying-Chun Lee, Georgia Chalvatzaki, Yuchen Cui, Ali Farhadi, Dieter Fox, Ranjay Krishna

entry.summary: MolmoSpaces is a large-scale open ecosystem for robot navigation and manipulation with 230k+ diverse indoor environments and 130k annotated object assets, from the Allen AI / UW / Georgia Tech team.

entry.title: Native Reasoning Models: Training Language Models to Reason on Unverifiable Data

author.name: Yuanfu Wang, Zhixuan Liu, Xiangtian Li, Chaochao Lu, Chao Yang

entry.summary: NRT (Native Reasoning Training) enables training reasoning models on unverifiable tasks by having the model generate its own reasoning traces from standard QA pairs, bypassing the need for human-annotated reasoning data or external verifiers.

entry.title: Extending Puzzle for Mixture-of-Experts Reasoning Models with Application to GPT-OSS Acceleration

author.name: Akhiad Bercovich, Nir Ailon, Vladimir Anisimov, Tomer Asida, Nave Assaf, Mohammad Dabbah, Ido Galil, Amnon Geifman, Yonatan Geifman, Izhak Golan, Roi Koren, Itay Levy, Zach Moshe, Pavlo Molchanov, Najeeb Nabwani, Mostofa Patwari, Omri Puny, Tomer Ronen, Itamar Schen, Elad Segal, Ido Shahaf, Oren Tropp, Ran Zilberstein, Ran El-Yaniv

entry.summary: Extends the Puzzle post-training NAS framework to GPT-OSS (OpenAI's open-source model), producing gpt-oss-puzzle-88B from the 120B model with 1.63x throughput speedup on 8xH100 while maintaining accuracy through MoE pruning, window attention, FP8 quantization, and RL recovery.

entry.title: SafeNeuron: Neuron-Level Safety Alignment for Large Language Models

author.name: Zhaoxin Wang, Jiaming Liang, Fengbin Zhu, Weixiang Zhao, Junfeng Fang, Jiayi Ji, Handing Wang, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: Proposes SafeNeuron, a neuron-level safety alignment framework that redistributes safety representations across the network rather than concentrating them in few parameters. Identifies safety-related neurons, freezes them during preference optimization, and adds safety neurons to improve robustness against neuron-level attacks.

entry.title: Unlearnable phases of matter

author.name: Tarun Advaith Kumar, Yijian Zou, Amir-Reza Negari, Roger G. Melko, Timothy H. Hsieh

entry.summary: Identifies fundamental limitations in machine learning by proving that non-trivial mixed-state phases of matter (specifically those with long-range conditional mutual information) are computationally hard to learn. Demonstrates that autoregressive neural networks fail to learn global properties of locally indistinguishable distributions.

entry.title: MonarchRT: Efficient Attention for Real-Time Video Generation

author.name: Krish Agarwal, Zhuoming Chen, Cheng Luo, Yongqi Chen, Haizhong Zheng, Xun Huang, Atri Rudra, Beidi Chen

entry.summary: Introduces MonarchRT for efficient attention in real-time video generation using Diffusion Transformers. Identifies that video attention combines periodic structure with dynamic sparse patterns, exceeding the capacity of top-k attention, and proposes Monarch-matrix-based attention. From Beidi Chen's group.

entry.title: LoopFormer: Elastic-Depth Looped Transformers for Latent Reasoning via Shortcut Modulation

author.name: Ahmadreza Jeddi, Marco Ciccone, Babak Taati

entry.summary: Proposes LoopFormer, a looped Transformer that can flexibly adapt its computational depth at inference time via a shortcut-consistency training scheme. This enables budget-conditioned reasoning where the model can trade off compute for quality, addressing a key limitation of fixed-iteration looped architectures.

entry.title: VLAW: Iterative Co-Improvement of Vision-Language-Action Policy and World Model

author.name: Yanjiang Guo, Tony Lee, Lucy Xiaoyang Shi, Jianyu Chen, Percy Liang, Chelsea Finn

entry.summary: VLAW proposes iterative co-improvement of VLA policies and world models through online interaction, using action-conditioned video generation models as learned simulators. Addresses the key challenge that existing world models lack physical fidelity for policy improvement, especially for contact-rich manipulation.

entry.title: LDA-1B: Scaling Latent Dynamics Action Model via Universal Embodied Data Ingestion

author.name: Jiangran Lyu, Kai Liu, Xuheng Zhang, Haoran Liao, Yusen Feng, Wenxuan Zhu, Tingrui Shen, Jiayi Chen, Jiazhao Zhang, Yifei Dong, Wenbo Cui, Senmao Qi, Shuo Wang, Yixin Zheng, Mi Yan, Xuesong Shi, Haoran Li, Dongbin Zhao, Ming-Yu Liu, Zhizheng Zhang, Li Yi, Yizhou Wang, He Wang

entry.summary: LDA-1B is a robot foundation model that scales through universal embodied data ingestion, jointly learning dynamics, policy, and visual forecasting from EI-30k (30k+ hours of heterogeneous embodied data). Assigns distinct roles to data of varying quality to maximize utility.

entry.title: Think Longer to Explore Deeper: Learn to Explore In-Context via Length-Incentivized Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Futing Wang, Jianhao Yan, Yun Luo, Ganqu Cui, Zhi Wang, Xiaoye Qu, Yue Zhang, Yu Cheng, Tao Lin

entry.summary: Proposes length-incentivized RL to address the 'Shallow Exploration Trap' where models fail to explore diverse reasoning paths during autoregressive generation. Grounded in State Coverage theory, shows that longer reasoning trajectories enable broader hypothesis exploration.

entry.title: Cross-Architecture Model Diffing with Crosscoders: Unsupervised Discovery of Differences Between LLMs

author.name: Thomas Jiralerspong, Trenton Bricken

entry.summary: Introduces Dedicated Feature Crosscoders (DFCs) for cross-architecture model diffing, enabling unsupervised discovery of differences between LLMs with different architectures. First application of crosscoders to cross-architecture comparison. Co-authored by Trenton Bricken (Anthropic).

entry.title: Spectra: Rethinking Optimizers for LLMs Under Spectral Anisotropy

author.name: Zhendong Huang, Hengjie Cao, Fang Dong, Ruijun Huang, Mengyi Chen, Yifeng Yang, Xin Zhang, Anrui Chen, Mingzhi Dong, Yujiang Wang, Jinlong Hou, Qin Lv, Robert P. Dick, Yuan Cheng, Fan Yang, Tun Lu, Li Shang

entry.summary: Spectra is a new optimizer for LLM training that addresses spectral anisotropy—where ~1.5% of spectral directions dominate optimizer statistics and suppress learning in the 'tail'. It suppresses the dominant spike subspace without amplifying noise-sensitive directions.

entry.title: Categorical Flow Maps

author.name: Daan Roos, Oscar Davis, Floor Eijkelboom, Michael Bronstein, Max Welling, \.Ismail \.Ilkan Ceylan, Luca Ambrogioni, Jan-Willem van de Meent

entry.summary: Introduces Categorical Flow Maps for accelerated few-step generation of categorical data via self-distillation in flow matching. The continuous simplex formulation enables existing distillation techniques and test-time compute scaling. Authors include Max Welling and Michael Bronstein.

entry.title: Optimizing Agent Planning for Security and Autonomy

author.name: Aashish Kolluri, Rishi Sharma, Manuel Costa, Boris K\"opf, Tobias Nie{\ss}en, Mark Russinovich, Shruti Tople, Santiago Zanella-B\'eguelin

entry.summary: Introduces autonomy metrics for AI agents under indirect prompt injection threats and designs a security-aware agent with richer human-in-the-loop interactions. Argues existing evaluations miss the benefit of system-level defenses in reducing reliance on human oversight. From Microsoft Research.

entry.title: PRIME: A Process-Outcome Alignment Benchmark for Verifiable Reasoning in Mathematics and Engineering

author.name: Xiangfeng Wang, Hangyu Guo, Yanlin Lai, Mitt Huang, Liang Zhao, Chengyuan Yao, Yinmin Zhang, Qi Han, Xiaoxiao Ren, Chun Yuan, Tong Xu, Zheng Ge, Xiangyu Zhang, Daxin Jiang

entry.summary: Introduces PRIME, a benchmark for evaluating whether model-based verifiers can detect correct answers produced from incorrect reasoning processes. Contains 2,530 college-level STEM problems and reveals that current verifiers struggle with process-outcome alignment.

entry.title: Stress Tests REVEAL Fragile Temporal and Visual Grounding in Video-Language Models

author.name: Sethuraman T V, Savya Khosla, Aditi Tiwari, Vidya Ganesh, Rakshana Jayaprakash, Aditya Jain, Vignesh Srinivasakumar, Onkar Kishor Susladkar, Srinidhi Sunkara, Aditya Shanmugham, Rakesh Vaideeswaran, Abbaas Alif Mohamed Nishar, Simon Jenni, Derek Hoiem

entry.summary: Introduces REVEAL, a diagnostic benchmark with five stress tests exposing fundamental weaknesses in Video-Language Models including temporal bias, language shortcuts, video sycophancy, and camera motion sensitivity. Shows leading models confidently describe reversed scenes as forward.

entry.title: CM2: Reinforcement Learning with Checklist Rewards for Multi-Turn and Multi-Step Agentic Tool Use

author.name: Zhen Zhang, Kaiqiang Song, Xun Wang, Yebowen Hu, Weixiang Yan, Chenyang Zhao, Henry Peng Zou, Haoyun Deng, Sathish Reddy Indurthi, Shujian Liu, Simin Ma, Xiaoyang Wang, Xin Eric Wang, Song Wang

entry.summary: CM2 proposes an RL framework for multi-turn, multi-step agentic tool use that replaces hard-to-define verifiable rewards with 'checklist rewards'—fine-grained binary criteria decomposed per turn. This addresses the challenge of training agents in realistic open-ended settings without executable environments.

entry.title: UMAP Is Spectral Clustering on the Fuzzy Nearest-Neighbor Graph

author.name: Yang Yang

entry.summary: Proves formally that UMAP performs spectral clustering on the fuzzy k-nearest-neighbor graph, establishing the exact theoretical connection between UMAP and classical spectral methods through contrastive learning equivalence.

entry.title: Learning to Forget Attention: Memory Consolidation for Adaptive Compute Reduction

author.name: Ibne Farabi Shihab, Sanjeda Akter, Anuj Sharma

entry.summary: Presents a biologically-inspired memory consolidation mechanism for transformers that reduces attention computation over time as recurring patterns become familiar. Key finding: 88% of attention operations in GPT-2 retrieve information already predictable from hidden states, and this redundancy persists during training.

entry.title: Mechanistic Evidence for Faithfulness Decay in Chain-of-Thought Reasoning

author.name: Donald Ye, Max Loffgren, Om Kotadia, Linus Wong

entry.summary: Proposes NLDD metric measuring whether individual CoT reasoning steps are faithful to the model's decision-making by corrupting steps and measuring confidence drops. Tests three model families and finds evidence of faithfulness decay.

entry.title: PACE: Prefix-Protected and Difficulty-Aware Compression for Efficient Reasoning

author.name: Ruixiang Feng, Yuntao Wen, Silin Zhou, Ke Shi, Yifan Wang, Ran Le, Zhenwei An, Zongchao Chen, Chen Yang, Guangyue Peng, Yiming Jia, Dongsheng Wang, Tao Zhang, Lisi Chen, Yang Song, Shen Gao, Shuo Shang

entry.summary: Proposes PACE, a dual-level framework that addresses 'overthinking' in Language Reasoning Models by applying prefix-protected optimization and difficulty-aware compression. Protects crucial early reasoning steps while compressing verbose later steps, achieving shorter outputs without accuracy loss.

entry.title: JEPA-VLA: Video Predictive Embedding is Needed for VLA Models

author.name: Shangchen Miao, Ningya Feng, Jialong Wu, Ye Lin, Xu He, Dong Li, Mingsheng Long

entry.summary: Proposes JEPA-VLA, arguing that video predictive embeddings (JEPA-style) are superior visual representations for VLA models compared to contrastive or reconstruction-based approaches. Shows improved sample efficiency and generalization for robotic manipulation.

entry.title: GigaBrain-0.5M*: a VLA That Learns From World Model-Based Reinforcement Learning

author.name: GigaBrain Team, Boyuan Wang, Chaojun Ni, Guan Huang, Guosheng Zhao, Hao Li, Jie Li, Jindi Lv, Jingyu Liu, Lv Feng, Mingming Yu, Peng Li, Qiuping Deng, Tianze Liu, Xinyu Zhou, Xinze Chen, Xiaofeng Wang, Yang Wang, Yifan Li, Yifei Nie, Yilong Li, Yukun Zhou, Yun Ye, Zhichao Liu, Zheng Zhu

entry.summary: GigaBrain-0.5M* is a Vision-Language-Action model trained via world model-based reinforcement learning, using video world models pre-trained on web-scale data to enhance spatiotemporal reasoning. Built upon GigaBrain-0.5 (pre-trained on 10,000+ hours of robotic manipulation data), it ranks first on the RoboChallenge benchmark.

entry.title: Response-Based Knowledge Distillation for Multilingual Jailbreak Prevention Unwittingly Compromises Safety

author.name: Max Zhang, Derek Liu, Kai Zhang, Joshua Franco, Haihao Liu

entry.summary: Examines knowledge distillation for multilingual jailbreak prevention, distilling refusal behaviors from OpenAI o1-mini into open-source models. Finds that while KD improves safety in some languages, it can compromise safety in others, revealing a tension between multilingual safety and distillation.

entry.title: LaCy: What Small Language Models Can and Should Learn is Not Just a Question of Loss

author.name: Szilvia Ujv\'ary, Louis B\'ethune, Pierre Ablin, Jo\~ao Monteiro, Marco Cuturi, Michael Kirchhof

entry.summary: Studies which tokens Small Language Models should learn during pretraining versus delegate to external sources via a special token. Finds that delegation decisions are not simply a function of loss — context and token type matter, suggesting capacity-aware training strategies.

entry.title: When and What to Ask: AskBench and Rubric-Guided RLVR for LLM Clarification

author.name: Jiale Zhao, Ke Fang, Lu Cheng

entry.summary: Introduces AskBench, a benchmark evaluating LLMs' ability to decide when and what to ask for clarification, with two settings: intent-deficient queries and queries with false premises. Proposes rubric-guided RLVR to improve clarification behavior without sacrificing task performance.

entry.title: On-Policy Context Distillation for Language Models

author.name: Tianzhu Ye, Li Dong, Xun Wu, Shaohan Huang, Furu Wei

entry.summary: Proposes On-Policy Context Distillation (OPCD), training a student model on its own generated trajectories while minimizing reverse KL divergence against a context-conditioned teacher. Demonstrates effectiveness for internalizing experiential knowledge and system prompts.

entry.title: More Haste, Less Speed: Weaker Single-Layer Watermark Improves Distortion-Free Watermark Ensembles

author.name: Ruibo Chen, Yihan Wu, Xuehao Cui, Jingqi Zhang, Heng Huang

entry.summary: Discovers that stronger individual-layer watermarks paradoxically weaken watermark ensembles by reducing token distribution entropy. Shows theoretically and empirically that deliberately weaker single-layer watermarks improve overall ensemble detectability.

entry.title: Detecting RLVR Training Data via Structural Convergence of Reasoning

author.name: Hongbo Zhang, Yue Yang, Jianhao Yan, Guangsheng Bao, Yue Zhang, Yue Zhang

entry.summary: Shows that RLVR training induces a distinctive behavioral signature: training prompts produce more rigid/similar generations while unseen prompts retain diversity. Introduces Min-kNN Distance, a black-box detector for identifying RLVR training data.

entry.title: Agentic Test-Time Scaling for WebAgents

author.name: Nicholas Lee, Lutfi Eren Erdogan, Chris Joseph John, Surya Krishnapillai, Michael W. Mahoney, Kurt Keutzer, Amir Gholami

entry.summary: CATTS introduces dynamic compute allocation for multi-step web agents at test time, finding that uniform per-step compute scaling quickly saturates in long-horizon tasks. They propose adaptive strategies including an LLM-based arbiter for better aggregation.

entry.title: HiFloat4 Format for Language Model Inference

author.name: Yuanyong Luo, Jing Huang, Yu Cheng, Ziwei Yu, Kaihua Zhang, Kehong Hong, Xinda Ma, Xin Wang, Anping Tong, Guipeng Hu, Yun Xu, Mehran Taghian, Peng Wu, Guanglin Li, Yunke Peng, Tianchi Hu, Minqi Chen, Michael Bi Mi, Hu Liu, Xiping Zhou, Junsong Wang, Qiang Lin, Heng Liao

entry.summary: HiFloat4 is a block floating-point format for LLM inference that packs 64 4-bit elements with 32 bits of shared scaling metadata (averaging 4.5 bits/value), featuring a three-level scaling hierarchy that achieves high accuracy on models including DeepSeek-V3.1.

entry.title: Krause Synchronization Transformers

author.name: Jingkun Liu, Yisong Yue, Max Welling, Yue Song

entry.summary: Krause Attention replaces softmax-based global aggregation with bounded-confidence consensus dynamics, promoting local synchronization over global mixing to address representation collapse and attention sink phenomena in deep transformers.

entry.title: PASCAL: A Phase-Aware Scheduling Algorithm for Serving Reasoning-based Large Language Models

author.name: Eunyeong Cho, Jehyeon Bang, Ranggi Hwang, Minsoo Rhu

entry.summary: Presents PASCAL, a phase-aware scheduling algorithm for serving reasoning LLMs that distinguishes between Chain-of-Thought reasoning phases and answer generation to reduce Time-To-First-Token while preserving quality of experience.

entry.title: Empirical Gaussian Processes

author.name: Jihao Andreas Lin, Sebastian Ament, Louis C. Tiao, David Eriksson, Maximilian Balandat, Eytan Bakshy

entry.summary: Introduces Empirical GPs, a framework for constructing data-driven Gaussian process priors by estimating mean and covariance functions from historical observations rather than handcrafting kernels. Demonstrates improved performance on Bayesian optimization benchmarks. Authors include researchers from Meta (Balandat, Bakshy).

entry.title: Active Zero: Self-Evolving Vision-Language Models through Active Environment Exploration

author.name: Jinghan He, Junfeng Fang, Feng Xiong, Zijun Yao, Fei Shen, Haiyun Guo, Jinqiao Wang, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: Proposes Active-Zero, a framework where vision-language models actively explore visual environments to find training data matched to their evolving capabilities. Uses three co-evolving agents: a Searcher, a Questioner, and a Reasoner, shifting from passive dataset interaction to active exploration.

entry.title: Barriers to Discrete Reasoning with Transformers: A Survey Across Depth, Exactness, and Bandwidth

author.name: Michelle Yuan, Weiyi Sun, Amir H. Rezaeian, Jyotika Singh, Sandip Ghoshal, Yao-Ting Wang, Miguel Ballesteros, Yassine Benajiba

entry.summary: Surveys theoretical barriers to discrete reasoning in transformers from three perspectives: circuit complexity, approximation theory, and communication complexity. Provides a unified account of why transformers struggle with symbolic computations.

entry.title: Composition-RL: Compose Your Verifiable Prompts for Reinforcement Learning of Large Language Models

author.name: Xin Xu, Clive Bai, Kai Yang, Tianhao Chen, Yangkun Chen, Weijie Liu, Hao Chen, Yang Wang, Saiyong Yang, Can Yang

entry.summary: Proposes Composition-RL, which automatically composes multiple easy problems into harder composite questions for RLVR training, addressing the problem of diminishing effective training data as easy problems reach pass-rate-1 during training.

entry.title: ABot-M0: VLA Foundation Model for Robotic Manipulation with Action Manifold Learning

author.name: Yandan Yang, Shuang Zeng, Tong Lin, Xinyuan Chang, Dekang Qi, Junjin Xiao, Haoyun Liu, Ronghan Chen, Yuzhi Chen, Dongjie Huo, Feng Xiong, Xing Wei, Zhiheng Ma, Mu Xu

entry.summary: Presents ABot-M0, a vision-language-action foundation model for robotic manipulation that builds a systematic data curation pipeline across six public datasets (6M+ trajectories). Addresses the 'one-brain, many-forms' challenge in embodied AI.

entry.title: Best of Both Worlds: Multimodal Reasoning and Generation via Unified Discrete Flow Matching

author.name: Onkar Susladkar, Tushar Prakash, Gayatri Deshmukh, Kiet A. Nguyen, Jiaxun Zhang, Adheesh Juvekar, Tianshu Bao, Lin Chai, Sparsh Mittal, Inderjit S Dhillon, Ismini Lourentzou

entry.summary: UniDFlow proposes a unified discrete flow-matching framework for multimodal understanding, generation, and editing. It uses task-specific low-rank adapters to decouple objectives and introduces reference-based multimodal preference alignment. Claims SOTA across eight benchmarks with strong zero-shot generalization.

entry.title: interwhen: A Generalizable Framework for Verifiable Reasoning with Test-time Monitors

author.name: Vishak K Bhat, Prateek Chanda, Ashmit Khandelwal, Maitreyi Swaroop, Vineeth N. Balasubramanian, Subbarao Kambhampati, Nagarajan Natarajan, Amit Sharma

entry.summary: Interwhen is a test-time verification framework that monitors reasoning model outputs against verifiers during generation, without requiring external step-by-step decomposition, enabling verified reasoning in high-stakes domains.

entry.title: Learn from Your Mistakes: Self-Correcting Masked Diffusion Models

author.name: Yair Schiff, Omer Belhasin, Roy Uziel, Guanghan Wang, Marianne Arriola, Gilad Turok, Michael Elad, Volodymyr Kuleshov

entry.summary: Proposes a self-correcting framework for masked diffusion models (MDMs) that trains the model to both unmask and correct tokens, addressing MDMs' fundamental limitation that once tokens are unmasked they remain fixed, leading to error accumulation.

entry.title: T3D: Few-Step Diffusion Language Models via Trajectory Self-Distillation with Direct Discriminative Optimization

author.name: Tunyu Zhang, Xinxi Zhang, Ligong Han, Haizhou Shi, Xiaoxiao He, Zhuowei Li, Hao Wang, Kai Xu, Akash Srivastava, Hao Wang, Vladimir Pavlovic, Dimitris N. Metaxas

entry.summary: Proposes T3D for few-step diffusion language model decoding using trajectory self-distillation with Direct Discriminative Optimization (DDO), a reverse-KL objective that promotes mode-seeking distillation for parallel text generation.

entry.title: Retrieval Heads are Dynamic

author.name: Yuping Lin, Zitao Li, Yue Xing, Pengfei He, Yingqian Cui, Yaliang Li, Bolin Ding, Jingren Zhou, Jiliang Tang

entry.summary: Investigates retrieval heads in LLMs from a dynamic perspective, showing they vary across timesteps during autoregressive generation and cannot be replaced by static retrieval heads. Establishes correlation between hidden states and dynamic retrieval head activation.

entry.title: P-GenRM: Personalized Generative Reward Model with Test-time User-based Scaling

author.name: Pinyi Zhang, Ting-En Lin, Yuchuan Wu, Jingyang Chen, Zongqi Wang, Hua Yang, Ze Xu, Fei Huang, Kai Zhang, Yongbin Li

entry.summary: Proposes P-GenRM, the first personalized generative reward model that adapts evaluation criteria to individual users via test-time user-based scaling. Transforms preference signals into structured evaluation chains with adaptive personas and scoring rubrics.

entry.title: Jailbreaking Leaves a Trace: Understanding and Detecting Jailbreak Attacks from Internal Representations of Large Language Models

author.name: Sri Durga Sai Sowmya Kadali, Evangelos E. Papalexakis

entry.summary: Studies jailbreaking from an interpretability perspective by analyzing how internal LLM representations differ between jailbreak and benign prompts. Finds that jailbreak attempts leave detectable traces in model internals, enabling detection.

entry.title: Credit Where It is Due: Cross-Modality Connectivity Drives Precise Reinforcement Learning for MLLM Reasoning

author.name: Zhengbo Jiao, Shaobo Wang, Zifan Zhang, Wei Wang, Bing Zhao, Hu Wei, Linfeng Zhang

entry.summary: Explores cross-modal attention connectivity in multimodal LLMs during RLVR training, finding that ~15% of tokens serve as visual-textual 'anchors' that ground reasoning. Proposes Anchor-Token RL to concentrate credit assignment on these critical tokens.

entry.title: Gradients Must Earn Their Influence: Unifying SFT with Generalized Entropic Objectives

author.name: Zecheng Wang, Deyuan Liu, Chunshan Li, Yupeng Zhang, Zhengyun Zhao, Dianhui Chu, Bingning Wang, Dianbo Sui

entry.summary: Unifies SFT objectives within a generalized deformed-log family, revealing a universal gate×error gradient structure that controls how much the model trusts its current prediction, addressing the plasticity-stability dilemma in token-level training.

entry.title: Sparse Semantic Dimension as a Generalization Certificate for LLMs

author.name: Dibyanayan Bandyopadhyay, Asif Ekbal

entry.summary: Proposes Sparse Semantic Dimension (SSD) as a complexity measure for LLMs based on sparse autoencoder analysis of activations, offering a theoretical explanation for why overparameterized LLMs generalize despite classical theory predicting overfitting.

entry.title: How Sampling Shapes LLM Alignment: From One-Shot Optima to Iterative Dynamics

author.name: Yurong Chen, Yu He, Michael I. Jordan, Fan Yao

entry.summary: Provides theoretical analysis of how sampling and reference policy choices affect LLM alignment through Identity Preference Optimization. Shows instance-dependent sampling yields stronger ranking guarantees and analyzes iterative alignment dynamics where learned policies feed back into future sampling.

entry.title: LAER-MoE: Load-Adaptive Expert Re-layout for Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Training

author.name: Xinyi Liu, Yujie Wang, Fangcheng Fu, Xuefeng Xiao, Huixia Li, Jiashi Li, Bin Cui

entry.summary: Introduces LAER-MoE with Fully Sharded Expert Parallel (FSEP), a new parallel paradigm that fully partitions expert parameters across devices and restores partial experts during training to address load imbalance in MoE training.

entry.title: Disentangling Ambiguity from Instability in Large Language Models: A Clinical Text-to-SQL Case Study

author.name: Angelo Ziletti, Leonardo D'Ambrosi

entry.summary: Proposes CLUES, a framework for clinical Text-to-SQL that disentangles two sources of output diversity: genuine input ambiguity (needing clarification) vs. model instability (needing human review). Uses Schur complement of a bipartite semantic graph to compute instability scores.

entry.title: Latent Generative Solvers for Generalizable Long-Term Physics Simulation

author.name: Zituo Chen, Haixu Wu, Sili Deng

entry.summary: Introduces Latent Generative Solvers (LGS), a two-stage framework for long-horizon PDE simulation that maps diverse PDE states into a shared latent space via a pretrained VAE and learns probabilistic dynamics with a Transformer trained by flow matching. Key innovations include an uncertainty knob for correcting rollout drift and flow forcing for improved long-term stability.

entry.title: From Atoms to Trees: Building a Structured Feature Forest with Hierarchical Sparse Autoencoders

author.name: Yifan Luo, Yang Zhan, Jiedong Jiang, Tianyang Liu, Mingrui Wu, Zhennan Zhou, Bin Dong

entry.summary: Proposes Hierarchical Sparse Autoencoders (HSAE) that jointly learn SAEs and parent-child feature relationships, capturing the hierarchical structure of features in LLMs through structural constraint loss and random feature perturbation.

entry.title: Think like a Scientist: Physics-guided LLM Agent for Equation Discovery

author.name: Jianke Yang, Ohm Venkatachalam, Mohammad Kianezhad, Sharvaree Vadgama, Rose Yu

entry.summary: KeplerAgent is an agentic framework for scientific equation discovery that mimics multi-step scientific reasoning—first inferring physical properties like symmetries, then using them to constrain candidate equations. This contrasts with LLM approaches that guess equations directly from data.

entry.title: SWE-MiniSandbox: Container-Free Reinforcement Learning for Building Software Engineering Agents

author.name: Danlong Yuan, Wei Wu, Zhengren Wang, Xueliang Zhao, Huishuai Zhang, Dongyan Zhao

entry.summary: SWE-MiniSandbox enables scalable RL training of software engineering agents without containers by using kernel-level isolation and lightweight pre-caching, substantially reducing storage and setup overhead.

entry.title: ABot-N0: Technical Report on the VLA Foundation Model for Versatile Embodied Navigation

author.name: Zedong Chu, Shichao Xie, Xiaolong Wu, Yanfen Shen, Minghua Luo, Zhengbo Wang, Fei Liu, Xiaoxu Leng, Junjun Hu, Mingyang Yin, Jia Lu, Yingnan Guo, Kai Yang, Jiawei Han, Xu Chen, Yanqing Zhu, Yuxiang Zhao, Xin Liu, Yirong Yang, Ye He, Jiahang Wang, Yang Cai, Tianlin Zhang, Li Gao, Liu Liu, Mingchao Sun, Fan Jiang, Chiyu Wang, Zhicheng Liu, Hongyu Pan, Honglin Han, Zhining Gu, Kuan Yang, Jianfang Zhang, Di Jing, Zihao Guan, Wei Guo, Guoqing Liu, Di Yang, Xiangpo Yang, Menglin Yang, Hongguang Xing, Weiguo Li, Mu Xu

entry.summary: Introduces ABot-N0, a unified Vision-Language-Action foundation model for embodied navigation that handles 5 core tasks (Point-Goal, Object-Goal, Instruction-Following, POI-Goal, Person-Following) with a hierarchical Brain-Action architecture. Trained on 16.9M expert trajectories across 7,802 3D scenes, achieving SOTA on 7 benchmarks.

entry.title: Towards Compressive and Scalable Recurrent Memory

author.name: Yunchong Song, Jushi Kai, Liming Lu, Kaixi Qiu, Zhouhan Lin

entry.summary: Introduces Elastic Memory, a novel recurrent memory architecture grounded in the HiPPO framework for online function approximation. Uses polynomial sampling for retrieval from compressed memory states, addressing the quadratic attention bottleneck for long contexts.

entry.title: Unifying Stable Optimization and Reference Regularization in RLHF

author.name: Li He, Qiang Qu, He Zhao, Stephen Wan, Dadong Wang, Lina Yao, Tongliang Liu

entry.summary: Introduces a unified regularization framework for RLHF that balances reward hacking prevention (KL to reference policy) with stable optimization (clipping toward current policy), addressing the implicit trade-off between these objectives.

entry.title: RAM-Net: Expressive Linear Attention with Selectively Addressable Memory

author.name: Kaicheng Xiao, Haotian Li, Liran Dong, Guoliang Xing

entry.summary: Introduces RAM-Net, a linear attention architecture with selectively addressable memory using high-dimensional sparse vectors as addresses, enabling exponential state size scaling without additional parameters and mitigating signal interference.

entry.title: Improving HPC Code Generation Capability of LLMs via Online Reinforcement Learning with Real-Machine Benchmark Rewards

author.name: Ryo Mikasa, Shun-ichiro Hayashi, Daichi Mukunoki, Tetsuya Hoshino, Takahiro Katagiri

entry.summary: Proposes an online RL approach that trains LLMs for HPC code generation by executing generated code on a supercomputer and using measured GFLOPS as reward. Introduces a Staged Quality-Diversity algorithm that progressively varies permitted optimization techniques. Addresses the underexplored area of runtime-performance-aware LLM training for scientific computing.

entry.title: Self-Supervised Learning via Flow-Guided Neural Operator on Time-Series Data

author.name: Duy Nguyen, Jiachen Yao, Jiayun Wang, Julius Berner, Animashree Anandkumar

entry.summary: Proposes Flow-Guided Neural Operator (FGNO) for self-supervised learning on time series, combining operator learning with flow matching. Treats corruption level as a learnable degree of freedom rather than fixed masking ratio, using STFT to unify different time resolutions. Authors include Animashree Anandkumar.

entry.title: Pretraining A Large Language Model using Distributed GPUs: A Memory-Efficient Decentralized Paradigm

author.name: Jinrui Zhang, Chaodong Xiao, Aoqi Wu, Xindong Zhang, Lei Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes SPES, a memory-efficient decentralized framework for pretraining MoE language models across distributed GPUs. Each node trains only a subset of experts, drastically reducing memory requirements while periodically synchronizing with other nodes.

entry.title: Thinking with Drafting: Optical Decompression via Logical Reconstruction

author.name: Jingxuan Wei, Honghao He, Caijun Jia, Siyuan Li, Zheng Sun, Yuhang Xu, Yuanyuan Lin, Linzhuang Sun, Yuchen Wu, Bihui Yu, Xiangxiang Zhang, Cheng Tan

entry.summary: Proposes Thinking with Drafting (TwD), which reconceptualizes visual reasoning as 'optical decompression' — reconstructing latent logical structures from visual tokens using a domain-specific language as intermediate representation. Addresses the precision paradox in multimodal reasoning.
