entry.title: Code2Worlds: Empowering Coding LLMs for 4D World Generation

author.name: Yi Zhang, Yunshuang Wang, Zeyu Zhang, Hao Tang

entry.summary: Introduces Code2Worlds, a framework formulating 4D world generation as language-to-simulation code using coding LLMs. Features dual-stream architecture separating object and environment generation, with a verification loop for physical fidelity.

entry.title: FAIL: Flow Matching Adversarial Imitation Learning for Image Generation

author.name: Yeyao Ma, Chen Li, Xiaosong Zhang, Han Hu, Weidi Xie

entry.summary: FAIL proposes using adversarial imitation learning for post-training of flow matching models, minimizing policy-expert divergence without explicit rewards or pairwise comparisons. It derives two algorithms: FAIL-PD using differentiable ODE solvers and FAIL-PG as a black-box alternative.

entry.title: When Agents Disagree With Themselves: Measuring Behavioral Consistency in LLM-Based Agents

author.name: Aman Mehta

entry.summary: Studies behavioral consistency of LLM agents across repeated runs, finding that ReAct-style agents produce 2-4.2 distinct action sequences per 10 runs. Inconsistency strongly predicts failure (80-92% accuracy for consistent vs 25-60% for inconsistent tasks). 69% of divergence occurs at step 2.

entry.title: The Pensieve Paradigm: Stateful Language Models Mastering Their Own Context

author.name: Xiaoyuan Liu, Tian Liang, Dongyang Ma, Deyu Zhou, Haitao Mi, Pinjia He, Yan Wang

entry.summary: Introduces StateLM, a foundation model with an internal reasoning loop for managing its own context through memory tools (context pruning, document indexing, note-taking). Trained to dynamically manage state rather than passively accepting context.

entry.title: HLA: Hadamard Linear Attention

author.name: Hanno Ackermann, Hong Cai, Mohsen Ghafoorian, Amirhossein Habibian

entry.summary: Proposes Hadamard Linear Attention (HLA), a new linear attention mechanism that applies nonlinearity after pairwise similarity computation (like softmax attention) rather than independently to queries and keys, enabling efficient computation.

entry.title: Security Threat Modeling for Emerging AI-Agent Protocols: A Comparative Analysis of MCP, A2A, Agora, and ANP

author.name: Zeynab Anbiaee, Mahdi Rabbani, Mansur Mirani, Gunjan Piya, Igor Opushnyev, Ali Ghorbani, Sajjad Dadkhah

entry.summary: Systematically analyzes security threats in four emerging AI agent communication protocols (MCP, A2A, Agora, ANP), developing a threat modeling framework and identifying protocol-specific vulnerabilities.

entry.title: Multimodal Fact-Level Attribution for Verifiable Reasoning

author.name: David Wan, Han Wang, Ziyang Wang, Elias Stengel-Eskin, Hyunji Lee, Mohit Bansal

entry.summary: MuRGAt is a benchmark for evaluating fact-level multimodal attribution in complex reasoning settings spanning video, audio, and other modalities, requiring models to ground individual claims to heterogeneous sources.

entry.title: UniT: Unified Multimodal Chain-of-Thought Test-time Scaling

author.name: Leon Liangyu Chen, Haoyu Ma, Zhipeng Fan, Ziqi Huang, Animesh Sinha, Xiaoliang Dai, Jialiang Wang, Zecheng He, Jianwei Yang, Chunyuan Li, Junzhe Sun, Chu Wang, Serena Yeung-Levy, Felix Juefei-Xu

entry.summary: Introduces UniT, a framework for multimodal chain-of-thought test-time scaling in unified models that handle both understanding and generation, enabling iterative reasoning and correction for complex spatial compositions.

entry.title: Evaluating Memory Structure in LLM Agents

author.name: Alina Shutova, Alexandra Olenina, Ivan Vinogradov, Anton Sinitsin

entry.summary: Proposes StructMemEval, a benchmark for evaluating LLM agents' ability to organize long-term memory hierarchically, going beyond simple fact recall to test complex memory structure capabilities.

entry.title: DICE: Diffusion Large Language Models Excel at Generating CUDA Kernels

author.name: Haolei Bai, Lingcheng Kong, Xueyi Chen, Jianmian Wang, Zhiqiang Tao, Huan Wang

entry.summary: Proposes DICE, a diffusion LLM approach for CUDA kernel generation, with a curated dataset (CuKe) and bi-phase reinforcement learning framework. Demonstrates that diffusion LLMs' parallel generation is well-suited for code with holistic structural planning needs.

entry.title: It's TIME: Towards the Next Generation of Time Series Forecasting Benchmarks

author.name: Zhongzheng Qiao, Sheng Pan, Anni Wang, Viktoriya Zhukova, Yong Liu, Xudong Jiang, Qingsong Wen, Mingsheng Long, Ming Jin, Chenghao Liu

entry.summary: Introduces TIME, a next-generation benchmark for time series foundation models with 50 fresh datasets and 98 forecasting tasks designed for zero-shot evaluation free from data leakage. Addresses limitations of existing benchmarks including reused data, compromised integrity, and misaligned task formulations.

entry.title: Insights on Muon from Simple Quadratics

author.name: Antoine Gonon, Andreea-Alexandra Mu\c{s}at, Nicolas Boumal

entry.summary: Analyzes the Muon optimizer on simple quadratic functions, showing existing single-step and worst-case analysis perspectives are insufficient. Identifies two phenomena affecting behavior on quadratics not captured by prevailing explanations.

entry.title: Who is the richest club in the championship? Detecting and Rewriting Underspecified Questions Improve QA Performance

author.name: Yunchong Huang, Gianni Barlacchi, Sandro Pezzelle

entry.summary: Shows that 16-50% of standard QA benchmark questions are underspecified, and LLMs perform significantly worse on them. Introduces a classifier for detecting underspecified questions and demonstrates that rewriting them into fully specified versions improves QA performance.

entry.title: Spatial Chain-of-Thought: Bridging Understanding and Generation Models for Spatial Reasoning Generation

author.name: Wei Chen, Yancheng Long, Mingqiao Liu, Haojie Ding, Yankai Yang, Hongyang Wei, Yi-Fan Zhang, Bin Wen, Fan Yang, Tingting Gao, Han Li, Long Chen

entry.summary: Proposes Spatial Chain-of-Thought (SCoT), a plug-and-play framework bridging MLLM reasoning with diffusion model generation for spatial reasoning. Trains diffusion models on interleaved text-coordinate data for layout awareness.

entry.title: HoloBrain-0 Technical Report

author.name: Xuewu Lin, Tianwei Lin, Yun Du, Hongyu Xie, Yiwei Jin, Jiawei Li, Shijie Wu, Qingze Wang, Mengdi Li, Mengao Zhao, Ziang Li, Chaodong Huang, Hongzhe Bi, Lichao Huang, Zhizhong Su

entry.summary: HoloBrain-0 is a VLA framework that explicitly incorporates robot embodiment priors (multi-view camera parameters, URDF) to enhance 3D spatial reasoning. Achieves SOTA on RoboTwin 2.0, LIBERO, and GenieSim benchmarks with an efficient 0.2B-parameter variant.

entry.title: Agent-Diff: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Enterprise API Tasks via Code Execution with State-Diff-Based Evaluation

author.name: Hubert M. Pysklo, Artem Zhuravel, Patrick D. Watson

entry.summary: Presents Agent-Diff, a benchmarking framework for evaluating LLM agents on real-world API tasks using state-diff-based evaluation. Balances sandboxed reproducibility with ecological validity by providing real API interfaces in a controlled environment.

entry.title: AgentLeak: A Full-Stack Benchmark for Privacy Leakage in Multi-Agent LLM Systems

author.name: Faouzi El Yagoubi, Ranwa Al Mallah, Godwin Badu-Marfo

entry.summary: Introduces AgentLeak, a benchmark for privacy leakage in multi-agent LLM systems covering 1,000 scenarios across healthcare, finance, legal, and corporate domains. Tests GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Mistral Large, and Llama 3.3 70B across 4,979 traces.

entry.title: Prototype Transformer: Towards Language Model Architectures Interpretable by Design

author.name: Yordan Yordanov, Matteo Forasassi, Bayar Menzat, Ruizhi Wang, Chang Qi, Markus Kaltenberger, Amine M'Charrak, Tommaso Salvatori, Thomas Lukasiewicz

entry.summary: Introduces the Prototype Transformer (ProtoT), an inherently interpretable autoregressive LM architecture using prototype vectors instead of standard self-attention. Prototypes automatically capture nameable concepts, providing built-in interpretability.

entry.title: When Should LLMs Be Less Specific? Selective Abstraction for Reliable Long-Form Text Generation

author.name: Shani Goren, Ido Galil, Ran El-Yaniv

entry.summary: Introduces Selective Abstraction, enabling LLMs to trade specificity for reliability by reducing detail of uncertain content rather than binary abstention. Decomposes responses into atomic claims and selectively abstracts uncertain ones.

entry.title: Stop Unnecessary Reflection: Training LRMs for Efficient Reasoning with Adaptive Reflection and Length Coordinated Penalty

author.name: Zewei Yu, Lirong Gao, Yuke Zhu, Bo Zheng, Sheng Guo, Haobo Wang, Junbo Zhao

entry.summary: Proposes ARLCP, an RL framework to reduce unnecessary reflection in large reasoning models. Finds that increasing problem complexity induces excessive, unproductive reflection that reduces accuracy while increasing token overhead.

entry.title: GPT-4o Lacks Core Features of Theory of Mind

author.name: John Muchovej, Amanda Royka, Shane Lee, Julian Jara-Ettinger

entry.summary: Tests GPT-4o on Theory of Mind using a cognitively-grounded evaluation framework that probes for coherent, domain-general causal models of mental states. Finds LLMs succeed at approximating human judgments but fail at logical consistency tests.

entry.title: MELINOE: Fine-Tuning Enables Memory-Efficient Inference for Mixture-of-Experts Models

author.name: Arian Raje, Anupam Nayak, Gauri Joshi

entry.summary: MELINOE fine-tunes MoE models to concentrate activation on fewer experts, reducing the need for expert offloading between CPU and GPU memory and addressing I/O latency bottlenecks for resource-constrained deployment.

entry.title: Predictive Associative Memory: Retrieval Beyond Similarity Through Temporal Co-occurrence

author.name: Jason Dury

entry.summary: Predictive Associative Memory (PAM) proposes retrieval based on temporal co-occurrence rather than similarity, using JEPA-style predictors to navigate associative structure in embedding space, complementing standard similarity-based memory.

entry.title: Divide and Learn: Multi-Objective Combinatorial Optimization at Scale

author.name: Esha Singh, Dongxia Wu, Chien-Yi Yang, Tajana Rosing, Rose Yu, Yi-An Ma

entry.summary: Reformulates multi-objective combinatorial optimization as an online learning problem with position-wise bandit subproblems, achieving regret bounds dependent on subproblem dimensionality rather than combinatorial space size, with 2-3 orders of magnitude efficiency gains.

entry.title: Can We Really Learn One Representation to Optimize All Rewards?

author.name: Chongyi Zheng, Royina Karegoudra Jayanth, Benjamin Eysenbach

entry.summary: Demystifies forward-backward (FB) representation learning for RL, clarifying when universal representations for arbitrary rewards can exist, what FB's objective actually optimizes, and the learning dynamics.

entry.title: DRACO: a Cross-Domain Benchmark for Deep Research Accuracy, Completeness, and Objectivity

author.name: Joey Zhong, Hao Zhang, Clare Southern, Jeremy Yang, Thomas Wang, Kate Jung, Shu Zhang, Denis Yarats, Johnny Ho, Jerry Ma

entry.summary: Presents DRACO, a benchmark for evaluating deep research systems across 10 domains and 40 countries, with tasks sampled from real Perplexity Deep Research usage patterns, graded on accuracy, completeness, presentation, and objectivity.

entry.title: Towards On-Policy SFT: Distribution Discriminant Theory and its Applications in LLM Training

author.name: Miaosen Zhang, Yishan Liu, Shuxia Lin, Xu Yang, Qi Dai, Chong Luo, Weihao Jiang, Peng Hou, Anxiang Zeng, Xin Geng, Baining Guo

entry.summary: Proposes Distribution Discriminant Theory (DDT) to quantify alignment between training data and model distribution, enabling On-Policy SFT through In-Distribution Finetuning and Hinted Decoding to bridge the SFT-RL gap.

entry.title: Charting Empirical Laws for LLM Fine-Tuning in Scientific Multi-Discipline Learning

author.name: Lintao Wang, Zhuqiang Lu, Yilin Zhu, Kun Hu, Zhenfei Yin, Shixiang Tang, Zhiyong Wang, Wanli Ouyang, Xinzhu Ma

entry.summary: Presents the first systematic study of multi-disciplinary LLM fine-tuning across five scientific domains, analyzing learning dynamics of full fine-tuning, LoRA, LoRA-MoE, and LoRA compositions. Discovers four empirical laws governing multi-discipline learning.

entry.title: SkillRater: Untangling Capabilities in Multimodal Data

author.name: Naveen Sahi, Jeremy Dohmann, Armen Aghajanyan, Akshat Shrivastava

entry.summary: Introduces SkillRater, a data curation framework that decomposes data quality into per-capability raters trained via meta-learning, with progressive selection rules that tighten thresholds over training stages.

entry.title: SpiralFormer: Looped Transformers Can Learn Hierarchical Dependencies via Multi-Resolution Recursion

author.name: Chengting Yu, Xiaobo Shu, Yadao Wang, Yizhen Zhang, Haoyi Wu, You Wu, Rujiao Long, Ziheng Chen, Yuchi Xu, Wenbo Su, Bo Zheng

entry.summary: Proposes SpiralFormer, a looped (recursive) Transformer that executes recurrence under a multi-resolution schedule, computing over compressed latent representations at different resolutions to learn hierarchical dependencies more efficiently.

entry.title: Protein Circuit Tracing via Cross-layer Transcoders

author.name: Darin Tsui, Kunal Talreja, Daniel Saeedi, Amirali Aghazadeh

entry.summary: Introduces ProtoMech, a framework for discovering computational circuits in protein language models using cross-layer transcoders that learn sparse latent representations jointly across layers, recovering 82-89% of original performance.

entry.title: PrefillShare: A Shared Prefill Module for KV Reuse in Multi-LLM Disaggregated Serving

author.name: Sunghyeon Woo, Hoseung Kim, Sunghwan Shim, Minjung Jo, Hyunjoon Jeong, Jeongtae Lee, Joonghoon Kim, Sungjae Lee, Baeseong Park, Se Jung Kwon, Dongsoo Lee

entry.summary: Proposes PrefillShare, a shared prefill module for multi-LLM disaggregated serving that eliminates redundant prefill computation and KV cache storage when multiple specialized models process the same prompt context in multi-agent systems.

entry.title: Oscillators Are All You Need: Irregular Time Series Modelling via Damped Harmonic Oscillators with Closed-Form Solutions

author.name: Yashas Shende (Ashoka University), Aritra Das (Ashoka University), Reva Laxmi Chauhan (Ashoka University), Arghya Pathak (Ashoka University), Debayan Gupta (Ashoka University)

entry.summary: Proposes replacing Neural ODEs with damped harmonic oscillators that have closed-form solutions for irregular time series modeling. This avoids the computational bottleneck of numerical ODE solvers while maintaining the ability to handle non-uniform time intervals in transformer-based architectures.

entry.title: Diffusion Alignment Beyond KL: Variance Minimisation as Effective Policy Optimiser

author.name: Zijing Ou, Jacob Si, Junyi Zhu, Ondrej Bohdal, Mete Ozay, Taha Ceritli, Yingzhen Li

entry.summary: Introduces VMPO for diffusion alignment, formulating it as minimizing variance of log importance weights from an SMC perspective rather than KL-based objectives. Proves the variance objective is minimized by the reward-tilted target and shows gradient equivalence with KL under on-policy sampling.

entry.title: Hierarchical Testing of a Hybrid Machine Learning-Physics Global Atmosphere Model

author.name: Ziming Chen, L. Ruby Leung, Wenyu Zhou, Jian Lu, Sandro W. Lubis, Ye Liu, Chuan-Chieh Chang, Bryce E. Harrop, Ya Wang, Mingshi Yang, Gan Zhang, Yun Qian

entry.summary: Evaluates NeuralGCM (a hybrid ML-physics atmospheric model) across multiple timescales including synoptic-scale phenomena, interannual variability, and out-of-distribution warming scenarios (+3K/+4K). Identifies sources of biases and assesses reliability for climate science applications.

entry.title: Echo: Towards Advanced Audio Comprehension via Audio-Interleaved Reasoning

author.name: Daiqing Wu, Xuan Zhang, Dongbao Yang, Jiashu Yao, Longfei Chen, Qingsong Liu, Sicheng Zhao, Can Ma, Yangyang Kang, Yu Zhou

entry.summary: Proposes audio-interleaved reasoning for Large Audio Language Models, treating audio as an active reasoning component rather than one-time encoded input. Uses a two-stage training with supervised fine-tuning for localization followed by RL for re-listening behavior.

entry.title: Mechanistic Interpretability for Large Language Model Alignment: Progress, Challenges, and Future Directions

author.name: Usman Naseem

entry.summary: Surveys mechanistic interpretability techniques applied to LLM alignment, covering circuit discovery, feature visualization, activation steering, and causal intervention. Examines how interpretability insights inform alignment strategies.

entry.title: SIGHT: Reinforcement Learning with Self-Evidence and Information-Gain Diverse Branching for Search Agent

author.name: Wenlin Zhong, Jinluan Yang, Yiquan Wu, Yi Liu, Jianhang Yao, Kun Kuang

entry.summary: Proposes SIGHT, an RL framework for search-based reasoning that addresses the 'tunnel vision' problem in multi-turn search through self-evidence support and information-gain driven diverse branching. Aims to prevent error accumulation from noisy early retrievals.

entry.title: Scaling Model and Data for Multilingual Machine Translation with Open Large Language Models

author.name: Yuzhe Shang, Pengzhi Gao, Wei Liu, Jian Luan, Jinsong Su

entry.summary: Develops MiLMMT-46, a multilingual MT system based on the Gemma3 model family that achieves top-tier translation across 46 languages. Investigates model scaling and data scaling effects through continual pretraining and instruction finetuning.

entry.title: Robot-DIFT: Distilling Diffusion Features for Geometrically Consistent Visuomotor Control

author.name: Yu Deng, Yufeng Jin, Xiaogang Jia, Jiahong Xue, Gerhard Neumann, Georgia Chalvatzaki

entry.summary: Robot-DIFT argues that a key bottleneck in generalizable manipulation is the structural mismatch between visual encoders (optimized for semantic invariance) and the geometric sensitivity needed for closed-loop control. Proposes distilling diffusion features that preserve dense spatial structure.

entry.title: ThinkRouter: Efficient Reasoning via Routing Thinking between Latent and Discrete Spaces

author.name: Xin Xu, Tong Yu, Xiang Chen, Haoliang Wang, Julian McAuley, Saayan Mitra

entry.summary: Proposes ThinkRouter, an inference-time confidence-aware routing mechanism that switches between latent and discrete reasoning spaces based on model confidence dynamics. Observes that incorrect reasoning trajectories contain fewer low-confidence steps.

entry.title: Detecting Overflow in Compressed Token Representations for Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Julia Belikova, Danila Rozhevskii, Dennis Svirin, Konstantin Polev, Alexander Panchenko

entry.summary: Defines and studies 'token overflow' in compressed token representations for RAG, where compression erases task-relevant content. Proposes methodology to detect overflow and finds that query-agnostic saturation statistics can reliably predict it.

entry.title: Benchmark Health Index: A Systematic Framework for Benchmarking the Benchmarks of LLMs

author.name: Longyuan Zhu, Hairan Hua, Linlin Miao, Bing Zhao

entry.summary: Introduces the Benchmark Health Index (BHI), a data-driven framework for auditing LLM evaluation benchmarks along three axes: capability discrimination, anti-saturation (remaining headroom), and impact across the community.

entry.title: When Models Examine Themselves: Vocabulary-Activation Correspondence in Self-Referential Processing

author.name: Zachary Pedram Dadfar

entry.summary: Studies whether LLM self-referential language reflects internal computation or confabulation, finding a specific activation direction that distinguishes self-referential from descriptive processing, orthogonal to the refusal direction.

entry.title: Temperature as a Meta-Policy: Adaptive Temperature in LLM Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Haoran Dang, Cuiling Lan, Hai Wan, Xibin Zhao, Yan Lu

entry.summary: Proposes TAMPO, a framework that treats temperature as a learnable meta-policy in LLM reinforcement learning, using a hierarchical two-loop process where the outer loop optimizes temperature based on reward signals.

entry.title: The Implicit Bias of Logit Regularization

author.name: Alon Beck, Yohai Bar Sinai, Noam Levi

entry.summary: Analyzes logit regularization (including label smoothing) in linear classification, showing it induces implicit bias of logit clustering around finite targets and drives weight vectors to align with Fisher's Linear Discriminant.

entry.title: PRIME: Policy-Reinforced Iterative Multi-agent Execution for Algorithmic Reasoning in Large Language Models

author.name: Jiawei Xu, Zhenyu Yu, Ziqian Bi, Minh Duc Pham, Xiaoyi Qu, Danyang Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes PRIME, a multi-agent framework for LLM algorithmic reasoning with executor, verifier, and coordinator agents optimized through group relative policy optimization. Introduces PRIME-Bench with 86 tasks across 12 categories with 51,600 instances.

entry.title: WavBench: Benchmarking Reasoning, Colloquialism, and Paralinguistics for End-to-End Spoken Dialogue Models

author.name: Yangzhuo Li, Shengpeng Ji, Yifu Chen, Tianle Liang, Haorong Ying, Yule Wang, Junbo Li, Jun Fang, Zhou Zhao

entry.summary: Introduces WavBench, a benchmark for evaluating spoken dialogue models across reasoning, colloquialism, and paralinguistics. Establishes a tripartite framework testing professional reasoning, colloquial understanding, and paralinguistic perception.

entry.title: STVG-R1: Incentivizing Instance-Level Reasoning and Grounding in Videos via Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Xiaowen Zhang, Zhi Gao, Licheng Jiao, Lingling Li, Qing Li

entry.summary: Proposes STVG-R1, using reinforcement learning to improve spatial-temporal video grounding by reformulating coordinate prediction as instance identification through visual prompting, avoiding cross-modal coordinate alignment.

entry.title: GHOST: Unmasking Phantom States in Mamba2 via Grouped Hidden-state Output-aware Selection & Truncation

author.name: Michael Menezes, Anastasios Kyrillidis

entry.summary: Introduces GHOST, a structured pruning framework for Mamba2 that approximates control-theoretic balanced truncation using only forward-pass statistics. Addresses inference overhead from Mamba2's expanded state dimension during autoregressive generation.

entry.title: MAPLE: Modality-Aware Post-training and Learning Ecosystem

author.name: Nikhil Verma, Minjung Kim, JooYoung Yoo, Kyung-Min Jin, Manasa Bharadwaj, Kevin Ferreira, Ko Keun Kim, Youngjoon Kim

entry.summary: Introduces MAPLE, a modality-aware post-training ecosystem for multimodal language models. Includes a benchmark annotating minimal signal combinations per task and MAPO, a policy optimization framework that stratifies batches by modality requirement to reduce gradient variance.

entry.title: scPilot: Large Language Model Reasoning Toward Automated Single-Cell Analysis and Discovery

author.name: Yiming Gao, Zhen Wang, Jefferson Chen, Mark Antkowiak, Mengzhou Hu, JungHo Kong, Dexter Pratt, Jieyuan Liu, Enze Ma, Zhiting Hu, Eric P. Xing

entry.summary: Presents scPilot, a framework enabling LLMs to perform single-cell RNA-seq analysis through 'omics-native reasoning' - conversing in natural language while directly inspecting biological data. Includes scBench benchmark with 9 curated datasets.

entry.title: Do MLLMs Really Understand Space? A Mathematical Reasoning Evaluation

author.name: Shuo Lu, Jianjie Cheng, Yinuo Xu, Yongcan Yu, Lijun Sheng, Peijie Wang, Siru Jiang, Yongguan Hu, Run Ling, Yihua Shao, Ao Ma, Wei Feng, Lingxiao He, Meng Wang, Qianlong Xie, Xingxing Wang, Ran He, Jian Liang

entry.summary: Introduces MathSpatial, a framework for evaluating and improving spatial reasoning in multimodal LLMs. Finds that while humans achieve >95% on textbook spatial reasoning, leading MLLMs fail to reach 60%, highlighting a fundamental weakness.

entry.title: AIR: Improving Agent Safety through Incident Response

author.name: Zibo Xiao, Jun Sun, Junjie Chen

entry.summary: Introduces AIR, the first incident response framework for LLM agent systems, defining a domain-specific language for managing the incident response lifecycle. Integrates detection, containment, and recovery into the agent execution loop.

entry.title: TSR: Trajectory-Search Rollouts for Multi-Turn RL of LLM Agents

author.name: Aladin Djuhera, Swanand Ravindra Kadhe, Farhan Ahmed, Holger Boche

entry.summary: Proposes TSR (Trajectory-Search Rollouts), which repurposes test-time scaling ideas for training-time trajectory generation in multi-turn RL of LLM agents. Uses lightweight tree-style search to construct high-quality training trajectories.

entry.title: "Sorry, I Didn't Catch That": How Speech Models Miss What Matters Most

author.name: Kaitlyn Zhou, Martijn Bartelds, Federico Bianchi, James Zou

entry.summary: Evaluates 15 ASR models from OpenAI, Deepgram, Google, and Microsoft on US street name transcription by diverse speakers, finding 44% average error rate. Shows mis-transcriptions cause routing errors that disproportionately affect non-English primary speakers.

entry.title: The Script Tax: Measuring Tokenization-Driven Efficiency and Latency Disparities in Multilingual Language Models

author.name: Aradhya Dixit, Shreem Dixit

entry.summary: Quantifies the 'script tax' in multilingual models: higher-fragmentation writing systems suffer ~3.4x more tokenization fragmentation, leading to 16.5x inference slowdown and significant information cost increases in mBERT and XLM-R.

entry.title: KBVQ-MoE: KLT-guided SVD with Bias-Corrected Vector Quantization for MoE Large Language Models

author.name: Zukang Xu, Zhixiong Zhao, Xing Hu, Zhixuan Chen, Dawei Yang

entry.summary: KBVQ-MoE proposes a compression method for MoE models combining KLT-guided SVD with bias-corrected vector quantization to handle redundant expert representations and quantization error.

entry.title: UltraLIF: Fully Differentiable Spiking Neural Networks via Ultradiscretization and Max-Plus Algebra

author.name: Jose Marie Antonio Mi\~noza

entry.summary: UltraLIF replaces heuristic surrogate gradients in spiking neural networks with ultradiscretization from tropical geometry, providing a principled differentiable framework using log-sum-exp as a soft-maximum that converges to hard thresholding.

entry.title: Credal Concept Bottleneck Models: Structural Separation of Epistemic and Aleatoric Uncertainty

author.name: Tanmoy Mukherjee, Marius Kloft, Pierre Marquis, Zied Bouraoui

entry.summary: Proposes credal-set formulation for concept bottleneck models that structurally separates epistemic uncertainty (size of the distribution set) from aleatoric uncertainty (noise within elements), addressing the correlation problem in standard approaches.

entry.title: The Energy of Falsehood: Detecting Hallucinations via Diffusion Model Likelihoods

author.name: Arpit Singh Gautam, Kailash Talreja, Saurabh Jha

entry.summary: DiffuTruth uses discrete text diffusion models for hallucination detection by corrupting claims with noise and measuring 'Semantic Energy'—the divergence between original and reconstructed text—treating factual truths as stable attractors.

entry.title: General and Efficient Steering of Unconditional Diffusion

author.name: Qingsong Wang, Mikhail Belkin, Yusu Wang

entry.summary: Proposes gradient-free steering of unconditional diffusion models using transferable concept vectors in activation space and noise alignment, avoiding per-step gradient computation during inference.

entry.title: Adaptive Milestone Reward for GUI Agents

author.name: Congmin Zheng, Xiaoyun Mo, Xinbei Ma, Qiqiang Lin, Yin Zhao, Jiachen Zhu, Xingyu Lou, Jun Wang, Zhaoxiang Wang, Weiwen Liu, Zhuosheng Zhang, Yong Yu, Weinan Zhang

entry.summary: ADMIRE proposes adaptive milestone rewards for training GUI agents via RL, dynamically distilling milestones from successful explorations and using asymmetric credit assignment to resolve the reward fidelity-density tradeoff.

entry.title: MiniCPM-SALA: Hybridizing Sparse and Linear Attention for Efficient Long-Context Modeling

author.name: MiniCPM Team, Wenhao An, Yingfa Chen, Yewei Fang, Jiayi Li, Xin Li, Yaohui Li, Yishan Li, Yuxuan Li, Biyuan Lin, Chuan Liu, Hezi Liu, Siyuan Liu, Hongya Lyu, Yinxu Pan, Shixin Ren, Xingyu Shen, Zhou Su, Haojun Sun, Yangang Sun, Zhen Leng Thai, Xin Tian, Rui Wang, Xiaorong Wang, Yudong Wang, Bo Wu, Xiaoyue Xu, Dong Xu, Shuaikang Xue, Jiawei Yang, Bowen Zhang, Jinqian Zhang, Letian Zhang, Shengnan Zhang, Xinyu Zhang, Xinyuan Zhang, Zhu Zhang, Hengyu Zhao, Jiacheng Zhao, Jie Zhou, Zihan Zhou, Shuo Wang, Chaojun Xiao, Xu Han, Zhiyuan Liu, Maosong Sun

entry.summary: Introduces MiniCPM-SALA, a 9B-parameter hybrid architecture combining sparse attention (InfLLM-V2) and linear attention (Lightning Attention) in a 1:3 ratio with hybrid positional encoding for efficient long-context modeling.

entry.title: Mitigating Mismatch within Reference-based Preference Optimization

author.name: Suqin Yuan, Xingrui Yu, Jiyang Zheng, Lei Feng, Dadong Wang, Ivor Tsang, Tongliang Liu

entry.summary: Identifies 'premature satisfaction' in DPO where the reference policy prematurely attenuates gradients on pessimistic pairs, and proposes a fix to mitigate this mismatch in reference-based preference optimization.

entry.title: Evaluating AGENTS.md: Are Repository-Level Context Files Helpful for Coding Agents?

author.name: Thibaud Gloaguen, Niels M\"undler, Mark M\"uller, Veselin Raychev, Martin Vechev

entry.summary: Evaluates whether repository-level context files (AGENTS.md) actually help coding agents, testing across SWE-bench tasks and novel issues. Provides the first rigorous investigation into a widespread but unvalidated practice.

entry.title: dVoting: Fast Voting for dLLMs

author.name: Sicheng Feng, Zigeng Chen, Xinyin Ma, Gongfan Fang, Xinchao Wang

entry.summary: Introduces dVoting, a fast voting technique for Diffusion Large Language Models (dLLMs) that boosts reasoning without training by leveraging the observation that token predictions are largely consistent across samples while performance depends on a small set of critical positions.

entry.title: Creative Ownership in the Age of AI

author.name: Annie Liang, Jay Lu

entry.summary: Proposes a formal framework for AI copyright infringement: a generative AI output infringes on a work if it could not have been generated without that work in the training corpus, modeled using closure operators.

entry.title: AM-FM: A Foundation Model for Ambient Intelligence Through WiFi

author.name: Guozhen Zhu, Yuqian Hu, Sakila Jayaweera, Weihang Gao, Wei-Hsiang Wang, Jiaxuan Zhang, Beibei Wang, Chenshu Wu, K. J. Ray Liu

entry.summary: Presents AM-FM, the first foundation model for ambient intelligence through WiFi, pre-trained on 9.2 million unlabeled Channel State Information samples collected over 439 days from 20 commercial device types. Enables human sensing (presence, activity, physiology) through existing WiFi infrastructure.

entry.title: The Magic Correlations: Understanding Knowledge Transfer from Pretraining to Supervised Fine-Tuning

author.name: Simin Fan, Dimitris Paparas, Natasha Noy, Binbin Xiong, Noveen Sachdeva, Berivan Isik

entry.summary: Investigates how language model capabilities transfer from pretraining to supervised fine-tuning, examining whether accuracy/confidence rankings persist, which benchmarks predict cross-stage performance, how transfer dynamics shift with scale, and calibration quality transfer.

entry.title: The Implicit Bias of Steepest Descent with Mini-batch Stochastic Gradient

author.name: Jichu Li, Xuan Tang, Difan Zou

entry.summary: Studies the implicit bias of mini-batch stochastic steepest descent in multi-class classification, characterizing how batch size, momentum, and variance reduction shape max-margin behavior under general norms, covering methods like SignSGD and Muon.

entry.title: Deep Kernel Fusion for Transformers

author.name: Zixi Zhang, Zhiwen Mo, Yiren Zhao, Robert Mullins

entry.summary: Proposes DeepFusionKernel, a deeply fused GPU kernel for SwiGLU MLP blocks in LLM inference that reduces HBM traffic and improves cache reuse, achieving up to 13.2% speedup on H100 integrated with SGLang.

entry.title: In-Context Function Learning in Large Language Models

author.name: Elif Akata, Konstantinos Voudouris, Vincent Fortuin, Eric Schulz

entry.summary: Studies in-context function learning in LLMs through controlled Gaussian Process experiments, evaluating how LLMs learn from demonstrations of multivariate functions and comparing against GP-regression and nearest-neighbor baselines.

entry.title: Learning Conditional Averages

author.name: Marco Bressan, Nataly Brukhim, Nicolo Cesa-Bianchi, Emmanuel Esposito, Yishay Mansour, Shay Moran, Maximilian Thiessen

entry.summary: Introduces the problem of learning conditional averages in the PAC framework, where the goal is to predict average labels over neighborhoods rather than individual labels. Provides a complete characterization of when this is learnable.

entry.title: Amortised and provably-robust simulation-based inference

author.name: Ayush Bharti, Charita Dellaporta, Yuga Hikida, Fran\c{c}ois-Xavier Briol

entry.summary: Introduces amortised simulation-based inference that is provably robust to outliers, combining generalised Bayesian inference with neural approximation of weighted score-matching loss. Achieves a combination of amortisation and robustness not previously available.

entry.title: Enforcing Reciprocity in Operator Learning for Seismic Wave Propagation

author.name: Caifeng Zou, Yaozhong Shi, Zachary E. Ross, Robert W. Clayton, Kamyar Azizzadenesheli

entry.summary: Introduces RENO, a transformer-based neural operator for seismic wave propagation that hard-codes the reciprocity principle through cross-attention and commutative operations, guaranteeing invariance under source-receiver swapping.

entry.title: PAC-Bayesian Generalization Guarantees for Fairness on Stochastic and Deterministic Classifiers

author.name: Julien Bastian (LabHC), Benjamin Leblanc (LabHC, IUF, MALICE), Pascal Germain (LabHC, IUF, MALICE), Amaury Habrard (LabHC, IUF, MALICE), Christine Largeron (LabHC), Guillaume Metzler (ERIC), Emilie Morvant (LabHC), Paul Viallard (MALT)

entry.summary: Derives PAC-Bayesian generalization bounds for fairness metrics, covering both stochastic and deterministic classifiers. Extends recent PAC-Bayes advances to provide fairness guarantees beyond the stochastic setting.

entry.title: Scale-Invariant Fast Convergence in Games

author.name: Taira Tsuchiya, Haipeng Luo, Shinji Ito

entry.summary: Develops scale-free and scale-invariant learning dynamics for games that achieve fast convergence without prior knowledge of utility scales. Obtains O(A_diff/T) convergence to Nash equilibrium in two-player zero-sum games.

entry.title: TADA! Tuning Audio Diffusion Models through Activation Steering

author.name: {\L}ukasz Staniszewski, Katarzyna Zaleska, Mateusz Modrzejewski, Kamil Deja

entry.summary: Uses activation patching to show that semantic musical concepts are controlled by a small shared subset of attention layers in audio diffusion models. Demonstrates Contrastive Activation Addition and Sparse Autoencoders can steer these layers to control specific audio attributes.

entry.title: Convex Markov Games and Beyond: New Proof of Existence, Characterization and Learning Algorithms for Nash Equilibria

author.name: Anas Barakat, Ioannis Panageas, Antonios Varvitsiotis

entry.summary: Studies Nash equilibria in General Utility Markov Games (extending convex Markov Games), proving NE coincide with fixed points of projected pseudo-gradient dynamics and providing convergence guarantees for learning algorithms.

entry.title: Are Aligned Large Language Models Still Misaligned?

author.name: Usman Naseem, Gautam Siddharth Kashyap, Rafiq Ali, Ebad Shabbir, Sushant Kumar Ray, Abdullah Mohammad, Agrima Seth

entry.summary: Introduces Mis-Align Bench for evaluating LLM misalignment across safety, value, and cultural dimensions simultaneously. Constructs a large dataset of 382K samples spanning 112 domains and evaluates multiple LLMs.

entry.title: Evaluating Alignment of Behavioral Dispositions in LLMs

author.name: Amir Taubenfeld, Zorik Gekhman, Lior Nezry, Omri Feldman, Natalie Harris, Shashir Reddy, Romina Stella, Ariel Goldstein, Marian Croak, Yossi Matias, Amir Feder

entry.summary: Introduces a framework for evaluating LLM behavioral dispositions using Situational Judgment Tests adapted from psychological questionnaires, with 2,500 validated SJTs and responses from 550 human participants.

entry.title: Which Feedback Works for Whom? Differential Effects of LLM-Generated Feedback Elements Across Learner Profiles

author.name: Momoka Furuhashi, Kouta Nakayama, Noboru Kawai, Takashi Kodama, Saku Sugawara, Kyosuke Takami

entry.summary: Studies how specific LLM-generated feedback elements (tone, information coverage) affect learning outcomes differently across student personality types. Conducts experiments with 321 high school students using GPT-5, finding that feedback effectiveness varies by Big Five personality traits.

entry.title: Query-focused and Memory-aware Reranker for Long Context Processing

author.name: Yuqing Li, Jiangnan Li, Mo Yu, Guoxuan Ding, Zheng Lin, Weiping Wang, Jie Zhou

entry.summary: Proposes a reranking framework that estimates passage-query relevance using attention scores from retrieval heads in LLMs. The lightweight approach requires only 4B parameter models and produces continuous relevance scores without Likert-scale supervision.

entry.title: Althea: Human-AI Collaboration for Fact-Checking and Critical Reasoning

author.name: Svetlana Churina, Kokil Jaidka, Anab Maulana Barik, Harshit Aneja, Cai Yang, Wynne Hsu, Mong Li Lee

entry.summary: Introduces Althea, a retrieval-augmented fact-checking system evaluated through both automated benchmarks and a 642-person user study. Compares different interaction modes for claim verification, achieving strong results on AVeriTeC benchmark.

entry.title: Ctrl&Shift: High-Quality Geometry-Aware Object Manipulation in Visual Generation

author.name: Penghui Ruan, Bojia Zi, Xianbiao Qi, Youze Huang, Rong Xiao, Pichao Wang, Jiannong Cao, Yuhui Shi

entry.summary: Presents Ctrl&Shift, a diffusion framework for geometry-consistent object manipulation in images/videos without explicit 3D reconstruction. Decomposes manipulation into two stages for background preservation and geometric consistency.

entry.title: LUVE : Latent-Cascaded Ultra-High-Resolution Video Generation with Dual Frequency Experts

author.name: Chen Zhao, Jiawei Chen, Hongyu Li, Zhuoliang Kang, Shilin Lu, Xiaoming Wei, Kai Zhang, Jian Yang, Ying Tai

entry.summary: Proposes LUVE, a three-stage framework for ultra-high-resolution video generation using dual frequency experts: low-res motion generation, latent-space upsampling, and high-res content refinement.

entry.title: Adaptive Debiasing Tsallis Entropy for Test-Time Adaptation

author.name: Xiangyu Wu, Dongming Jiang, Feng Yu, Yueying Tian, Jiaqi Tang, Qing-Guo Chen, Yang Yang, Jianfeng Lu

entry.summary: Shows that Tsallis Entropy is better suited than Shannon Entropy for test-time adaptation of CLIP models due to CLIP's built-in distribution bias. Proposes Adaptive Debiasing Tsallis Entropy (ADTE) that customizes entropy parameters per sample.

entry.title: Learning to Manipulate Anything: Revealing Data Scaling Laws in Bounding-Box Guided Policies

author.name: Yihao Wu, Jinming Ma, Junbo Tan, Yanzhao Yu, Shoujie Li, Mingliang Zhou, Diyun Xiang, Xueqian Wang

entry.summary: Investigates data scaling laws in semantic manipulation by using bounding-box instructions to specify target objects. Introduces Label-UMI, a handheld segmentation device with automated annotation pipeline, and a semantic-motion-decoupled framework for generalization.

entry.title: Efficient Segment Anything with Depth-Aware Fusion and Limited Training Data

author.name: Yiming Zhou, Xuenjie Xie, Panfeng Li, Albrecht Kunz, Ahmad Osman, Xavier Maldague

entry.summary: Shows that augmenting EfficientViT-SAM with monocular depth priors achieves higher accuracy than the original while training on only 0.1% of SA-1B data. Demonstrates that depth cues provide strong geometric priors for segmentation.

entry.title: Budget-Constrained Agentic Large Language Models: Intention-Based Planning for Costly Tool Use

author.name: Hanbing Liu, Chunhao Tian, Nan An, Ziyuan Wang, Pinyan Lu, Changyuan Yu, Qi Qi

entry.summary: Proposes INTENT, an inference-time planning framework for budget-constrained tool-augmented LLM agents. Uses an intention-aware hierarchical world model to anticipate tool costs and guide decisions under strict monetary budgets.

entry.title: What if Agents Could Imagine? Reinforcing Open-Vocabulary HOI Comprehension through Generation

author.name: Zhenlong Yuan, Xiangyan Qu, Jing Tang, Rui Chen, Lei Sun, Ruidong Chen, Hongwei Yu, Chengxuan Qian, Xiangxiang Chu, Shuo Li, Yuyin Zhou

entry.summary: Proposes ImagineAgent, an agentic framework for open-vocabulary human-object interaction detection that uses cognitive maps and generative imagination (including diffusion models) to address cross-modal hallucinations and occlusion ambiguity.

entry.title: AgentNoiseBench: Benchmarking Robustness of Tool-Using LLM Agents Under Noisy Condition

author.name: Ruipeng Wang, Yuxin Chen, Yukai Wang, Chang Wu, Junfeng Fang, Xiaodong Cai, Qi Gu, Hui Su, An Zhang, Xiang Wang, Xunliang Cai, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: Introduces AgentNoiseBench, a framework for evaluating LLM agent robustness under noisy real-world conditions. Categorizes environmental noise types and systematically benchmarks how noise degrades agent performance compared to idealized settings.

entry.title: Distributionally Robust Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning via Robust Value Factorization

author.name: Chengrui Qu, Christopher Yeh, Kishan Panaganti, Eric Mazumdar, Adam Wierman

entry.summary: Introduces Distributionally Robust IGM (DrIGM) for cooperative multi-agent RL, ensuring robust value factorization under environmental uncertainties from sim-to-real gaps. Provides theoretical guarantees and practical algorithms.

entry.title: Learning to Configure Agentic AI Systems

author.name: Aditya Taparia, Som Sagar, Ransalu Senanayake

entry.summary: Introduces ARC (Agentic Resource & Configuration learner), which uses RL to dynamically configure LLM agent systems (workflows, tools, token budgets, prompts) per query, replacing fixed templates or hand-tuned heuristics.

entry.title: Predicting LLM Output Length via Entropy-Guided Representations

author.name: Huanyi Xie, Yubin Chen, Liangyu Wang, Lijie Hu, Di Wang

entry.summary: Introduces a lightweight framework for predicting LLM output length using the model's own hidden states, with Entropy-Guided Token Pooling for static prediction and Progressive Length Prediction for dynamic estimation. Reduces computational waste from padding.

entry.title: Revis: Sparse Latent Steering to Mitigate Object Hallucination in Large Vision-Language Models

author.name: Jialin Wu, Wei Shi, Han Shen, Peigui Qi, Kunsheng Tang, Zhicong Huang, Binghao Wang, Zhou Yang

entry.summary: Proposes REVIS, a training-free framework that mitigates object hallucination in vision-language models by re-activating suppressed visual information through orthogonal projection and sparse intervention at specific network depths.

entry.title: Value Alignment Tax: Measuring Value Trade-offs in LLM Alignment

author.name: Jiajun Chen, Hua Shen

entry.summary: Introduces Value Alignment Tax (VAT), a framework measuring how alignment interventions propagate effects across interconnected values. Uses Schwartz value theory to analyze how optimizing for one value affects the broader value system.

entry.title: Visualizing and Benchmarking LLM Factual Hallucination Tendencies via Internal State Analysis and Clustering

author.name: Nathan Mao, Varun Kaushik, Shreya Shivkumar, Parham Sharafoleslami, Kevin Zhu, Sunishchal Dev

entry.summary: Introduces FalseCite, a dataset for studying hallucinations induced by misleading citations, and analyzes internal hidden states of hallucinating models, finding that hidden state clustering can distinguish hallucinated from truthful responses.

entry.title: From Noise to Order: Learning to Rank via Denoising Diffusion

author.name: Sajad Ebrahimi, Bhaskar Mitra, Negar Arabzadeh, Ye Yuan, Haolun Wu, Fattane Zarrinkalam, Ebrahim Bagheri

entry.summary: Proposes a denoising diffusion-based generative approach to learning-to-rank that models the full joint distribution over features and relevance labels, hypothesizing that generative ranking produces more robust models than discriminative approaches.

entry.title: Compiler-Guided Inference-Time Adaptation: Improving GPT-5 Programming Performance in Idris

author.name: Minda Li, Bhaskar Krishnamachari

entry.summary: Evaluates GPT-5's programming ability in the low-resource language Idris, finding poor baseline performance (22/56) compared to Python (45/50), then tests compiler-guided iterative refinement strategies to improve performance.

entry.title: Stop Tracking Me! Proactive Defense Against Attribute Inference Attack in LLMs

author.name: Dong Yan, Jian Liang, Ran He, Tieniu Tan

entry.summary: Proposes a defense framework combining fine-grained anonymization (TRACE) with inference-preventing optimization (RPS) to protect against LLM-based attribute inference attacks on user-generated text.

entry.title: Analytical Search

author.name: Yiteng Tu, Shuo Miao, Weihang Su, Yiqun Liu, Qingyao Ai

entry.summary: Proposes 'Analytical Search' as a new IR paradigm for complex analytical information needs (trend analysis, causal assessment), going beyond document ranking or simple RAG-based QA to support structured reasoning over corpus-scale data.

entry.title: Zooming without Zooming: Region-to-Image Distillation for Fine-Grained Multimodal Perception

author.name: Lai Wei, Liangbo He, Jun Lan, Lingzhong Dong, Yutong Cai, Siyuan Li, Huijia Zhu, Weiqiang Wang, Linghe Kong, Yue Wang, Zhuosheng Zhang, Weiran Huang

entry.summary: Proposes Region-to-Image Distillation that internalizes the benefits of agentic zooming (iterative crop-and-examine) into a single forward pass of an MLLM through training-time distillation from zoomed micro-crops.

entry.title: The Observer Effect in World Models: Invasive Adaptation Corrupts Latent Physics

author.name: Christian Intern\`o, Jumpei Yamaguchi, Loren Amdahl-Culleton, Markus Olhofer, David Klindt, Barbara Hammer

entry.summary: Proposes PhyIP, a non-invasive evaluation protocol for testing whether neural world models internalize physical laws, finding that invasive adaptation (fine-tuning/probes) can corrupt learned representations and confound evaluation.

entry.title: Olmix: A Framework for Data Mixing Throughout LM Development

author.name: Mayee F. Chen, Tyler Murray, David Heineman, Matt Jordan, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Christopher R\'e, Luca Soldaini, Kyle Lo

entry.summary: Presents Olmix, a framework for data mixing throughout LM development that addresses evolving domain sets and data constraints through comprehensive empirical study of design choices.

entry.title: CADET: Context-Conditioned Ads CTR Prediction With a Decoder-Only Transformer

author.name: David Pardoe, Neil Daftary, Miro Furtado, Aditya Aiyer, Yu Wang, Liuqing Li, Tao Song, Lars Hertel, Young Jin Yun, Senthil Radhakrishnan, Zhiwei Wang, Tommy Li, Khai Tran, Ananth Nagarajan, Ali Naqvi, Yue Zhang, Renpeng Fang, Avi Romascanu, Arjun Kulothungun, Deepak Kumar, Praneeth Boda, Fedor Borisyuk, Ruoyan Wang

entry.summary: Presents CADET, a decoder-only transformer for ads click-through rate prediction deployed at LinkedIn, introducing context-conditioned processing, offline-online consistency mechanisms, and industrial-scale deployment insights.

entry.title: Dopamine: Brain Modes, Not Brains

author.name: Shervin Ghasemlou

entry.summary: Proposes Dopamine, a PEFT method inspired by neuromodulation that learns per-neuron thresholds and gains rather than weight updates, treating adaptation as mode selection/rescaling of existing computations.

entry.title: Using predictive multiplicity to measure individual performance within the AI Act

author.name: Karolin Frohnapfel, Mara Seyfert, Sebastian Bordt, Ulrike von Luxburg, Kristof Meding

entry.summary: Argues that predictive multiplicity—the existence of many models with similar accuracy but different individual predictions—conflicts with the EU AI Act's requirement for individual-level performance reporting, and proposes using this concept to measure individual performance.

entry.title: Improved state mixing in higher-order and block diagonal linear recurrent networks

author.name: Igor Dubinin, Antonio Orvieto, Felix Effenberger

entry.summary: Explores increasing expressivity of linear recurrent networks through higher-order recurrence (H-LRU) mixing multiple past states and block-diagonal structure (BD-LRU) enabling dense intra-block interactions, while maintaining efficiency.

entry.title: Function-Space Decoupled Diffusion for Forward and Inverse Modeling in Carbon Capture and Storage

author.name: Xin Ju, Jiachen Yao, Anima Anandkumar, Sally M. Benson, Gege Wen

entry.summary: Presents Fun-DDPS, combining function-space diffusion models with differentiable neural operator surrogates for forward and inverse modeling in Carbon Capture and Storage. Decouples the diffusion prior from physics-consistent surrogate guidance for geological parameter recovery. Authors include Anima Anandkumar.

entry.title: The Cost of Learning under Multiple Change Points

author.name: Tomer Gafni, Garud Iyengar, Assaf Zeevi

entry.summary: Studies online learning with multiple change points, identifying 'endogenous confounding' as a phenomenon causing catastrophic failure in classical detection methods. Proposes Anytime Tracking CUSUM (ATC) algorithms that balance ignoring small shifts with quickly reacting to significant ones.

entry.title: DMAP: A Distribution Map for Text

author.name: Tom Kempton, Julia Rozanova, Parameswaran Kamalaruban, Maeve Madigan, Karolina Wresilo, Yoann L. Launay, David Sutton, Stuart Burrell

entry.summary: Introduces DMAP, a method mapping text via LLM next-token distributions to samples in the unit interval encoding rank and probability information. Enables model-agnostic text analysis going beyond perplexity by accounting for distributional context.

entry.title: Moonshine v2: Ergodic Streaming Encoder ASR for Latency-Critical Speech Applications

author.name: Manjunath Kudlur, Evan King, James Wang, Pete Warden

entry.summary: Introduces Moonshine v2, a streaming ASR encoder using an ergodic attention mechanism for low-latency speech recognition on edge devices, addressing the quadratic complexity bottleneck of full-attention transformers for streaming applications.

entry.title: MetaMem: Evolving Meta-Memory for Knowledge Utilization through Self-Reflective Symbolic Optimization

author.name: Haidong Xin, Xinze Li, Zhenghao Liu, Yukun Yan, Shuo Wang, Cheng Yang, Yu Gu, Ge Yu, Maosong Sun

entry.summary: Proposes MetaMem, augmenting LLM memory systems with self-evolving meta-memory that teaches models how to utilize memorized knowledge. Iteratively distills transferable knowledge utilization experiences across tasks via symbolic optimization.

entry.title: Advancing AI Trustworthiness Through Patient Simulation: Risk Assessment of Conversational Agents for Antidepressant Selection

author.name: Md Tanvir Rouf Shawon, Mohammad Sabik Irbaz, Hadeel R. A. Elyazori, Keerti Reddy Resapu, Yili Lin, Vladimir Franzuela Cardenas, Farrokh Alemi, Kevin Lybarger

entry.summary: Introduces a patient simulator for scalable evaluation of healthcare conversational agents, grounded in the NIST AI Risk Management Framework. The simulator generates realistic patient interactions varying across medical, linguistic, and behavioral dimensions to identify hallucinations and risk patterns in antidepressant selection scenarios.

entry.title: Do Large Language Models Adapt to Language Variation across Socioeconomic Status?

author.name: Elisa Bassignana, Mike Zhang, Dirk Hovy, Amanda Cercas Curry

entry.summary: Studies whether LLMs adapt their linguistic style to different socioeconomic status communities, finding that models fail to mirror the diverse linguistic norms of various SES groups. Uses a novel Reddit/YouTube dataset stratified by SES.

entry.title: Mask What Matters: Mitigating Object Hallucinations in Multimodal Large Language Models with Object-Aligned Visual Contrastive Decoding

author.name: Boqi Chen, Xudong Liu, Jianing Qiu

entry.summary: Improves visual contrastive decoding for reducing object hallucinations in multimodal LLMs by constructing object-aligned auxiliary views using self-supervised Vision Transformer attention. The method is prompt-agnostic and model-agnostic.

entry.title: Electrostatics-Inspired Surface Reconstruction (EISR): Recovering 3D Shapes as a Superposition of Poisson's PDE Solutions

author.name: Diego Pati\~no, Knut Peterson, Kostas Daniilidis, David K. Han

entry.summary: Presents EISR, a novel surface reconstruction approach using Poisson's equation from electrostatics. Uses Green's functions for closed-form parametric solutions and leverages PDE linearity for efficient optimization.

entry.title: H-WM: Robotic Task and Motion Planning Guided by Hierarchical World Model

author.name: Wenyuan Chen, Jinbang Huang, Oscar Pang, Zhiyuan Li, Xiao Hu, Lingfeng Zhang, Zhanguang Zhang, Mark Coates, Tongtong Cao, Xingyue Quan, Yingxue Zhang

entry.summary: H-WM proposes a hierarchical world model that jointly predicts logical and visual state transitions within a unified bi-level architecture for robotic task and motion planning. Bridges traditional symbolic planning with visual perception.

entry.title: HAIC: Humanoid Agile Object Interaction Control via Dynamics-Aware World Model

author.name: Dongting Li, Xingyu Chen, Qianyang Wu, Bo Chen, Sikai Wu, Hanyu Wu, Guoyao Zhang, Liang Li, Mingliang Zhou, Diyun Xiang, Jianzhu Ma, Qiang Zhang, Renjing Xu

entry.summary: HAIC is a framework for humanoid robot interaction with underactuated objects (those with independent dynamics and non-holonomic constraints). Uses a dynamics predictor that estimates high-order object states from proprioceptive history alone, without external state estimation.

entry.title: ReplicatorBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Replicability in Social and Behavioral Sciences

author.name: Bang Nguyen, Dominik So\'os, Qian Ma, Rochana R. Obadage, Zack Ranjan, Sai Koneru, Timothy M. Errington, Shakhlo Nematova, Sarah Rajtmajer, Jian Wu, Meng Jiang

entry.summary: Introduces ReplicatorBench, a benchmark for evaluating LLM agents' ability to assess scientific paper replicability in social and behavioral sciences. Unlike prior work focusing on computational reproduction, it includes non-replicable papers and evaluates the replication process.

entry.title: TRACER: Trajectory Risk Aggregation for Critical Episodes in Agentic Reasoning

author.name: Sina Tayebati, Divake Kumar, Nastaran Darabi, Davide Ettori, Ranganath Krishnan, Amit Ranjan Trivedi

entry.summary: Introduces TRACER, a trajectory-level uncertainty metric for multi-turn tool-using AI agents. Combines content-aware surprisal with situational-awareness signals and tool-grounded coherence to detect critical failure episodes that local confidence measures miss.

entry.title: Beyond Parameter Arithmetic: Sparse Complementary Fusion for Distribution-Aware Model Merging

author.name: Weihong Lin, Lin Sun, Qilong Shi, Aomufei Yuan, Yuxuan Tian, Zhengyang Wang, Guangxiang Zhao, Xiangzheng Zhang, Tong Yang

entry.summary: Proposes SCF-RKL, a model merging framework that controls functional interference through sparse, distribution-aware updates using reverse KL divergence, instead of parameter-space heuristics that cause degraded generation.

entry.title: PuYun-LDM: A Latent Diffusion Model for High-Resolution Ensemble Weather Forecasts

author.name: Lianjun Wu, Shengchen Zhu, Yuxuan Liu, Liuyu Kai, Xiaoduan Feng, Duomin Wang, Wenshuo Liu, Jingxuan Zhang, Kelvin Li, Bin Wang

entry.summary: Introduces PuYun-LDM, a latent diffusion model for high-resolution ensemble weather forecasting. Proposes a 3D Masked AutoEncoder addressing diffusability challenges specific to meteorological data with inter-variable spectral heterogeneity.

entry.title: Neutral Prompts, Non-Neutral People: Quantifying Gender and Skin-Tone Bias in Gemini Flash 2.5 Image and GPT Image 1.5

author.name: Roberto Balestri

entry.summary: Quantifies gender and skin-tone bias in Gemini Flash 2.5 Image and GPT Image 1.5, finding >96% 'default white' bias in neutral prompts. Tests 3,200 images using Monk, PERLA, and Fitzpatrick skin-tone scales.

entry.title: Small Updates, Big Doubts: Does Parameter-Efficient Fine-tuning Enhance Hallucination Detection ?

author.name: Xu Hu, Yifan Zhang, Songtao Wei, Chen Zhao, Qiannan Li, Bingzhe Li, Feng Chen

entry.summary: Systematically investigates how parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods affect hallucination detection in LLMs, finding that PEFT can both help and hurt depending on the detection method and backbone.

entry.title: RooflineBench: A Benchmarking Framework for On-Device LLMs via Roofline Analysis

author.name: Zhen Bi, Xueshu Chen, Luoyang Sun, Yuhang Yao, Qing Shen, Jungang Lou, Cheng Deng

entry.summary: RooflineBench provides a systematic framework based on the Roofline model for benchmarking on-device LLM inference, introducing Relative Inference Potential as a metric comparing efficiency across architectures and hardware.

entry.title: TS-Memory: Plug-and-Play Memory for Time Series Foundation Models

author.name: Sisuo Lyu, Siru Zhong, Tiegang Chen, Weilin Ruan, Qingxiang Liu, Taiqiang Lv, Qingsong Wen, Raymond Chi-Wing Wong, Yuxuan Liang

entry.summary: TS-Memory augments frozen time series foundation models with a lightweight memory adapter trained via parametric distillation from a kNN teacher, addressing distribution shift without catastrophic forgetting.

entry.title: Evaluating LLM Safety Under Repeated Inference via Accelerated Prompt Stress Testing

author.name: Keita Broadwater

entry.summary: Introduces Accelerated Prompt Stress Testing (APST), a depth-oriented evaluation framework that repeatedly samples identical prompts to surface latent failure modes like hallucinations and refusal inconsistencies under sustained use.

entry.title: Accelerating Robotic Reinforcement Learning with Agent Guidance

author.name: Haojun Chen, Zili Zou, Chengdong Ma, Yaoxiang Pu, Haotong Zhang, Yuanpei Chen, Yaodong Yang

entry.summary: Introduces Agent-guided Policy Search (AGPS) that replaces human supervisors with a multimodal agent for real-world robotic RL training, addressing the scalability bottleneck of human-in-the-loop methods.

entry.title: On the Complexity of Offline Reinforcement Learning with $Q^\star$-Approximation and Partial Coverage

author.name: Haolin Liu, Braham Snyder, Chen-Yu Wei

entry.summary: Studies offline RL under Q*-approximation and partial coverage, proving that Q*-realizability and Bellman completeness are insufficient for sample-efficient offline RL, and introduces a framework characterizing intrinsic complexity.

entry.title: Provably Efficient Algorithms for S- and Non-Rectangular Robust MDPs with General Parameterization

author.name: Anirudh Satheesh, Ziyi Chen, Furong Huang, Heng Huang

entry.summary: Studies robust MDPs with general policy parameterization under s-rectangular and non-rectangular uncertainty sets, proving novel Lipschitz properties and introducing a multilevel Monte Carlo gradient estimator with O(ε⁻²) sample complexity.

entry.title: FedGRPO: Privately Optimizing Foundation Models with Group-Relative Rewards from Domain Client

author.name: Gongxi Zhu, Hanlin Gu, Lixin Fan, Qiang Yang, Yuxing Han

entry.summary: Proposes FedGRPO, a privacy-preserving framework for federated foundation models that reformulates knowledge transfer from client models to server as an RL-style evaluation process using Group Relative Policy Optimization.

entry.title: Few-Shot Design Optimization by Exploiting Auxiliary Information

author.name: Arjun Mani, Carl Vondrick, Richard Zemel

entry.summary: Introduces a Bayesian Optimization setting where experiments generate high-dimensional auxiliary information alongside the objective, with a history of prior tasks available. Proposes methods to learn useful representations of auxiliary information for efficient optimization.

entry.title: Decentralized Non-convex Stochastic Optimization with Heterogeneous Variance

author.name: Hongxu Chen, Ke Wei, Luo Luo

entry.summary: Proposes D-NSS, a decentralized optimization algorithm with node-specific sampling that achieves sample complexity depending on arithmetic mean of local standard deviations rather than worst-case, with matching lower bounds.

entry.title: Safety Beyond the Training Data: Robust Out-of-Distribution MPC via Conformalized System Level Synthesis

author.name: Anutam Srinivasan, Antoine Leeman, Glen Chou

entry.summary: Presents a framework for robust out-of-distribution planning using conformal prediction with system level synthesis for MPC, providing theoretical guarantees on coverage and robustness under distributional drift when using learned dynamics models.

entry.title: Cross-Modal Robustness Transfer (CMRT): Training Robust Speech Translation Models Using Adversarial Text

author.name: Abderrahmane Issam, Yusuf Can Semerci, Jan Scholtes, Gerasimos Spanakis

entry.summary: Proposes Cross-Modal Robustness Transfer (CMRT) for speech translation, transferring adversarial robustness from text to speech domain without expensive adversarial speech data generation. Shows E2E speech translation models are vulnerable to morphological attacks.

entry.title: Arbitrary Ratio Feature Compression via Next Token Prediction

author.name: Yufan Liu, Daoyuan Ren, Zhipeng Zhang, Wenyang Luo, Bing Li, Weiming Hu, Stephen Maybank

entry.summary: Proposes Arbitrary Ratio Feature Compression using auto-regressive next-token prediction, supporting any compression ratio with a single model instead of requiring dedicated models for each ratio.

entry.title: RI-Mamba: Rotation-Invariant Mamba for Robust Text-to-Shape Retrieval

author.name: Khanh Nguyen, Dasith de Silva Edirimuni, Ghulam Mubashar Hassan, Ajmal Mian

entry.summary: Proposes RI-Mamba, the first rotation-invariant state-space model for point clouds, applied to text-to-shape retrieval. Uses global/local reference frames and Hilbert sorting for meaningful geometric token sequences.

entry.title: GSO-SLAM: Bidirectionally Coupled Gaussian Splatting and Direct Visual Odometry

author.name: Jiung Yeon, Seongbo Ha, Hyeonwoo Yu

entry.summary: Proposes GSO-SLAM, a real-time monocular dense SLAM system using Gaussian splatting with bidirectional coupling between visual odometry and Gaussian representation within an EM framework.

entry.title: EO-VAE: Towards A Multi-sensor Tokenizer for Earth Observation Data

author.name: Nils Lehmann, Yi Wang, Zhitong Xiong, Xiaoxiang Zhu

entry.summary: EO-VAE is a multi-sensor variational autoencoder designed as a foundational tokenizer for Earth observation data, using a single model with dynamic hypernetworks to encode and reconstruct flexible channel combinations across different sensor types.

entry.title: General Humanoid Whole-Body Control via Pretraining and Fast Adaptation

author.name: Zepeng Wang, Jiangxing Wang, Shiqing Yao, Yu Zhang, Ziluo Ding, Ming Yang, Yuxuan Wang, Haobin Jiang, Chao Ma, Xiaochuan Shi, Zongqing Lu

entry.summary: FAST introduces a general humanoid whole-body control framework using Parseval-Guided Residual Policy Adaptation for fast adaptation to out-of-distribution motions while mitigating catastrophic forgetting through orthogonality and KL constraints.

entry.title: When would Vision-Proprioception Policies Fail in Robotic Manipulation?

author.name: Jingxian Lu, Wenke Xia, Yuxuan Wu, Zhiwu Lu, Di Hu

entry.summary: Investigates when vision-proprioception policies fail in robotic manipulation through temporally controlled experiments. Finds that during motion transitions requiring target localization, vision plays a limited role because the policy gravitates toward proprioceptive signals that offer faster loss reduction.

entry.title: Affordance-Graphed Task Worlds: Self-Evolving Task Generation for Scalable Embodied Learning

author.name: Xiang Liu, Sen Cui, Guocai Yao, Zhong Cao, Jingheng Ma, Min Zhang, Changshui Zhang

entry.summary: AGT-World autonomously constructs interactive simulated environments and robot task policies from real-world observations using a structured affordance graph. Enables hierarchical decomposition of complex goals into physically grounded subtasks with closed-loop execution.

entry.title: Pushing Forward Pareto Frontiers of Proactive Agents with Behavioral Agentic Optimization

author.name: Yihang Yao, Zhepeng Cen, Haohong Lin, Shiqi Liu, Zuxin Liu, Jiacheng Zhu, Zhang-Wei Hong, Laixi Shi, Ding Zhao

entry.summary: Proposes BAO, an agentic RL framework for training proactive LLM agents that balances task performance with user engagement using Pareto optimization. Addresses the trade-off between passive instruction-following and over-soliciting user feedback.

entry.title: The Five Ws of Multi-Agent Communication: Who Talks to Whom, When, What, and Why -- A Survey from MARL to Emergent Language and LLMs

author.name: Jingdi Chen, Hanqing Yang, Zongjun Liu, Carlee Joe-Wong

entry.summary: Comprehensive survey of multi-agent communication organized through the 'Five Ws' framework, tracing evolution from MARL through emergent language to LLM-based agents. Covers who, what, when, why of agent communication.

entry.title: Right for the Wrong Reasons: Epistemic Regret Minimization for Causal Rung Collapse in LLMs

author.name: Edward Y. Chang

entry.summary: Formalizes 'Rung Collapse' where autoregressive training fails to distinguish association from intervention in causal reasoning. Proposes Epistemic Regret Minimization to penalize errors in causal reasoning independently of task success.

entry.title: Tiny Recursive Reasoning with Mamba-2 Attention Hybrid

author.name: Wenlong Wang, Fergal Reid

entry.summary: Investigates replacing Transformer blocks in TRM (Tiny Recursive Reasoning) with Mamba-2 hybrid operators for abstract reasoning tasks. Finds the hybrid improves on ARC-AGI-1 while maintaining parameter parity (~7M parameters).

entry.title: Sci-CoE: Co-evolving Scientific Reasoning LLMs via Geometric Consensus with Sparse Supervision

author.name: Xiaohan He, Shiyang Feng, Songtao Huang, Lei Bai, Bin Wang, Bo Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes Sci-CoE, a co-evolving framework for scientific reasoning LLMs using geometric consensus with sparse supervision. Models co-evolve as solver and verifier through a transition from sparse to unsupervised learning.

entry.title: Assessing LLM Reliability on Temporally Recent Open-Domain Questions

author.name: Pushwitha Krishnappa, Amit Das, Vinija Jain, Tathagata Mukherjee, Aman Chadha

entry.summary: Introduces RECOM, a benchmark of 15,000 recent Reddit questions (from September 2025) to test LLM reliability on temporally recent information, finding a 'semantic-lexical paradox' where models achieve high semantic similarity but low lexical overlap.

entry.title: Finding the Cracks: Improving LLMs Reasoning with Paraphrastic Probing and Consistency Verification

author.name: Weili Shi, Dongliang Guo, Lehan Yang, Tianlong Wang, Hanzhang Yuan, Sheng Li

entry.summary: PPCV framework improves LLM reasoning by using paraphrastic probing to identify critical tokens and consistency verification to refine reasoning trajectories, reducing error accumulation in multi-step reasoning.

entry.title: Differentially Private and Communication Efficient Large Language Model Split Inference via Stochastic Quantization and Soft Prompt

author.name: Yujie Gu, Richeng Jin, Xiaoyu Ji, Yier Jin, Wenyuan Xu

entry.summary: DEL proposes a differentially private LLM split inference framework using stochastic quantization and soft prompts to reduce communication overhead while maintaining privacy guarantees.

entry.title: ReaDy-Go: Real-to-Sim Dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting Simulation for Environment-Specific Visual Navigation with Moving Obstacles

author.name: Seungyeon Yoo, Youngseok Jang, Dabin Kim, Youngsoo Han, Seungwoo Jung, H. Jin Kim

entry.summary: ReaDy-Go is a real-to-sim simulation pipeline using 3D Gaussian Splatting that generates photorealistic dynamic scenarios for robot visual navigation training in specific target environments.

entry.title: AmbiBench: Benchmarking Mobile GUI Agents Beyond One-Shot Instructions in the Wild

author.name: Jiazheng Sun, Mingxuan Li, Yingying Zhang, Jiayang Niu, Yachen Wu, Ruihan Jin, Shuyu Lei, Pengrongrui Tan, Zongyu Zhang, Ruoyi Wang, Jiachen Yang, Boyu Yang, Jiacheng Liu, Xin Peng

entry.summary: Introduces AmbiBench, the first benchmark for evaluating mobile GUI agents on ambiguous instructions requiring active clarification during execution, moving beyond the idealized assumption of complete, unequivocal instructions.

entry.title: Choose Your Agent: Tradeoffs in Adopting AI Advisors, Coaches, and Delegates in Multi-Party Negotiation

author.name: Kehang Zhu, Lithium Thain, Vivian Tsai, James Wexler, Crystal Qian

entry.summary: Behavioral experiment (N=243) studying tradeoffs when humans interact with LLM-powered Advisor, Coach, and Delegate modalities in multi-party bargaining games, examining adoption patterns and outcomes.

entry.title: Learning beyond Teacher: Generalized On-Policy Distillation with Reward Extrapolation

author.name: Wenkai Yang, Weijie Liu, Ruobing Xie, Kai Yang, Saiyong Yang, Yankai Lin

entry.summary: Theoretically shows that on-policy distillation (OPD) is a special case of dense KL-constrained RL, and proposes Generalized OPD with flexible reference model and reward scaling factor for improved knowledge distillation.

entry.title: DeepGen 1.0: A Lightweight Unified Multimodal Model for Advancing Image Generation and Editing

author.name: Dianyi Wang, Ruihang Li, Feng Han, Chaofan Ma, Wei Song, Siyuan Wang, Yibin Wang, Yi Xin, Hongjian Liu, Zhixiong Zhang, Shengyuan Ding, Tianhang Wang, Zhenglin Cheng, Tao Lin, Cheng Jin, Kaicheng Yu, Jingjing Chen, Wenjie Wang, Zhongyu Wei, Jiaqi Wang

entry.summary: Presents DeepGen 1.0, a lightweight 5B unified multimodal model for image generation and editing using Stacked Channel Bridging (SCB) to extract hierarchical VLM features with 'think tokens' for structured guidance.

entry.title: Patch the Distribution Mismatch: RL Rewriting Agent for Stable Off-Policy SFT

author.name: Jiacheng Wang, Ping Jian, Zhen Yang, Zirong Chen, Keren Liao, Zhongbin Guo

entry.summary: Proposes using RL to rewrite downstream training data before supervised fine-tuning to address distribution mismatch and catastrophic forgetting. Cast as an RL problem to align rewritten data with the model's natural generation distribution.

entry.title: How Well Do Large-Scale Chemical Language Models Transfer to Downstream Tasks?

author.name: Tatsuya Sagawa, Ryosuke Kojima

entry.summary: Evaluates whether scaling training resources for Chemical Language Models improves downstream molecular property prediction, finding that while pretraining loss decreases, downstream performance shows limited improvement.

entry.title: Universal Diffusion-Based Probabilistic Downscaling

author.name: Roberto Molinaro, Niall Siegenheim, Henry Martin, Mark Frey, Niels Poulsen, Philipp Seitz, Marvin Vincent Gabler

entry.summary: Introduces a universal diffusion-based downscaling framework that transforms deterministic low-resolution weather forecasts into probabilistic high-resolution predictions in a zero-shot manner across different upstream weather models.

entry.title: Amortized Molecular Optimization via Group Relative Policy Optimization

author.name: Muhammad bin Javaid, Hasham Hussain, Ashima Khanna, Berke Kisin, Jonathan Pirnay, Alexander Mitsos, Dominik G. Grimm, Martin Grohe

entry.summary: Introduces GRXForm for amortized molecular optimization using Group Relative Policy Optimization, adapting a pre-trained Graph Transformer for sequential molecular modifications. Identifies high variance from heterogeneous starting structures as a key failure mode of existing model-based approaches.

entry.title: Adaptive Power Iteration Method for Differentially Private PCA

author.name: Ta Duy Nguyem, Alina Ene, Huy Le Nguyen

entry.summary: Studies differentially private PCA using an adaptive power iteration method with a filtering technique that adapts to the coherence parameter of the input matrix, providing better-than-worst-case utility guarantees for low-coherence matrices.

entry.title: Free Lunch for Stabilizing Rectified Flow Inversion

author.name: Chenru Wang, Beier Zhu, Chi Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes Proximal-Mean Inversion (PMI) for stabilizing rectified flow inversion, addressing error accumulation across timesteps that degrades reconstruction and editing quality in RF-based generative models.

entry.title: Iskra: A System for Inverse Geometry Processing

author.name: Ana Dodik, Ahmed H. Mahmoud, Justin Solomon

entry.summary: Proposes Iskra, a system for differentiating through geometry processing problems, compatible with ML frameworks. Exploits existing fast solvers (local-global, ADMM) and uses the adjoint method for efficient backward passes.

entry.title: ExStrucTiny: A Benchmark for Schema-Variable Structured Information Extraction from Document Images

author.name: Mathieu Sibue, Andres Mu\~noz Garza, Samuel Mensah, Pranav Shetty, Zhiqiang Ma, Xiaomo Liu, Manuela Veloso

entry.summary: Introduces ExStrucTiny, a benchmark for evaluating VLMs on schema-variable structured information extraction from documents. Tests the ability to perform holistic, fine-grained extraction across diverse document types with flexible schemas.

entry.title: Selective Prior Synchronization via SYNC Loss

author.name: Ishan Mishra, Jiajie Li, Deepak Mishra, Jinjun Xiong

entry.summary: Proposes SYNC Loss for selective prediction, arguing that the selective prior (uncertainty information) generated by post-hoc methods should be synchronized during training rather than only used at inference time.

entry.title: Clutt3R-Seg: Sparse-view 3D Instance Segmentation for Language-grounded Grasping in Cluttered Scenes

author.name: Jeongho Noh, Tai Hyoung Rhee, Eunho Lee, Jeongyun Kim, Sunwoo Lee, Ayoung Kim

entry.summary: Presents Clutt3R-Seg, a zero-shot pipeline for 3D instance segmentation in cluttered scenes using hierarchical instance trees. Enables language-grounded robotic grasping by leveraging noisy masks as informative cues rather than trying to refine them.

entry.title: WorldTree: Towards 4D Dynamic Worlds from Monocular Video using Tree-Chains

author.name: Qisen Wang, Yifan Zhao, Jia Li

entry.summary: Proposes WorldTree for monocular 4D dynamic reconstruction using Temporal Partition Trees for hierarchical temporal decomposition and Spatial Ancestral Chains for spatial dynamics.

entry.title: DreamID-Omni: Unified Framework for Controllable Human-Centric Audio-Video Generation

author.name: Xu Guo, Fulong Ye, Qichao Sun, Liyang Chen, Bingchuan Li, Pengze Zhang, Jiawei Liu, Songtao Zhao, Qian He, Xiangwang Hou

entry.summary: DreamID-Omni unifies human-centric audio-video generation tasks (reference-based generation, video editing, audio-driven animation) in a single framework with a Symmetric Conditional Diffusion Transformer, enabling disentangled control over multiple character identities and voice timbres.

entry.title: ExtremControl: Low-Latency Humanoid Teleoperation with Direct Extremity Control

author.name: Ziyan Xiong, Lixing Fang, Junyun Huang, Kashu Yamazaki, Hao Zhang, Chuang Gan

entry.summary: ExtremControl is a low-latency humanoid teleoperation framework that operates directly on SE(3) poses of extremity links, uses Cartesian-space mapping to avoid full-body retargeting, and incorporates velocity feedforward for rapid reactive control.

entry.title: Cross-Fitting-Free Debiased Machine Learning with Multiway Dependence

author.name: Kaicheng Chen, Harold D. Chiang

entry.summary: Develops asymptotic theory for debiased machine learning estimators in GMM models with multiway clustered dependence without requiring cross-fitting. Shows valid inference can be achieved through Neyman-orthogonal moments with localization-based empirical processes.

entry.title: Dissecting Subjectivity and the "Ground Truth" Illusion in Data Annotation

author.name: Sheza Munir, Benjamin Mah, Krisha Kalsi, Shivani Kapania, Julian Posada, Edith Law, Ding Wang, Syed Ishtiaque Ahmed

entry.summary: Systematic literature review analyzing 149 papers on data annotation practices, examining how the 'ground truth' paradigm treats human disagreement as noise rather than signal. Covers 2020-2025 across seven premier venues and identifies mechanisms that facilitate a 'consensus trap' in annotation.

entry.title: Neuro-Symbolic Multitasking: A Unified Framework for Discovering Generalizable Solutions to PDE Families

author.name: Yipeng Huang, Dejun Xu, Zexin Lin, Zhenzhong Wang, Min Jiang

entry.summary: Proposes a neuro-symbolic multitasking framework that discovers generalizable, interpretable closed-form solutions for PDE families through symbolic regression, bridging neural solvers' speed with symbolic interpretability.

entry.title: PhyNiKCE: A Neurosymbolic Agentic Framework for Autonomous Computational Fluid Dynamics

author.name: E Fan, Lisong Shi, Zhengtong Li, Chih-yung Wen

entry.summary: Introduces PhyNiKCE, a neurosymbolic agentic framework for autonomous CFD simulation. Addresses 'context poisoning' where LLM agents generate physically invalid configurations by decoupling neural planning from symbolic physics verification.

entry.title: Pedagogically-Inspired Data Synthesis for Language Model Knowledge Distillation

author.name: Bowei He, Yankai Chen, Xiaokun Zhang, Linghe Kong, Philip S. Yu, Xue Liu, Chen Ma

entry.summary: Proposes a pedagogically-inspired knowledge distillation framework (IOA pipeline) that systematically identifies student model deficiencies, organizes progressive curricula, and adapts difficulty, inspired by educational principles.

entry.title: SAM3-LiteText: An Anatomical Study of the SAM3 Text Encoder for Efficient Vision-Language Segmentation

author.name: Chengxi Zeng, Yuxuan Jiang, Ge Gao, Shuai Wang, Duolikun Danier, Bin Zhu, Stevan Rudinac, David Bull, Fan Zhang

entry.summary: Performs large-scale analysis of text encoder redundancy in vision-language segmentation models like SAM3, analyzing 404,796 prompts. Finds severe over-provisioning in text encoders since segmentation prompts are short and structured.

entry.title: Improving Medical Visual Reinforcement Fine-Tuning via Perception and Reasoning Augmentation
